sentences.zh: 邵續

translations.literal: Shao Xu
translations.idiomatic: Shao Xu

sentences.zh: 邵續，字嗣祖，魏郡安陽人也。

translations.literal: Shao Xu, style name Sizu, was a man of Anyang in Wei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Xu, courtesy Sizu, came from Anyang in Wei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 父乘，散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Shao Cheng was gentleman attendant at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Shao Cheng, had risen to gentleman attendant at leisure.

sentences.zh: 續樸素有志烈，博覽經史，善談理義，妙解天文。

translations.literal: Shao Xu was plain and frugal and possessed of fierce resolve; he read widely in the classics and histories, was skilled at discussing principle and meaning, and had a subtle grasp of astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Xu lived plainly and held fierce convictions; he read deeply across the classics and histories, argued principle with ease, and read the stars with uncommon skill.

sentences.zh: 初為成都王穎參軍，穎將討長沙王乂，續諫曰：「續聞兄弟如左右手，今明公當天下之敵，而欲去一手乎？

translations.literal: At first he served as army adviser to Prince Chengdu Sima Ying; when Ying was about to campaign against Prince Changsha Sima Yi, Shao Xu remonstrated: "I have heard that brothers are like the left and right hand; now the enlightened lord faces the empire's foes—would you wish to remove one hand?
translations.idiomatic: He first joined the staff of Prince Chengdu, Sima Ying. When Ying prepared to strike Prince Changsha, Sima Yi, Shao Xu urged him: "They say brothers are like a man's two hands; you stand against the whole realm—would you willingly cut one off?

sentences.zh: 續竊惑之。

translations.literal: Shao Xu privately was perplexed by this.
translations.idiomatic: He could not fathom Ying's plan.

sentences.zh: 」穎不納。

translations.literal: Ying did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Ying would not listen.

sentences.zh: 後為苟晞參軍，除沁水令。

translations.literal: Later he served as army adviser to Gou Xi and was appointed magistrate of Qinshui.
translations.idiomatic: He later served on Gou Xi's staff and was named magistrate of Qinshui.

sentences.zh: 時天下漸亂，續去縣還家，糾合亡命，得數百人。

translations.literal: At that time the realm was gradually falling into chaos; Shao Xu left the county and returned home, rallied fugitives from the law, and obtained several hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: As the empire slid toward chaos, Shao Xu quit his post, went home, and gathered several hundred outlaws around him.

sentences.zh: 王浚假續綏集將軍、樂陵太守，屯厭次，以續子乂為督護。

translations.literal: Wang Jun provisionally appointed Shao Xu General Who Pacifies and Gathers and prefect of Leling, garrisoned Yanci, and appointed Shao Xu's son Shao Yi as chief of staff.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun named him acting General Who Pacifies and Gathers and prefect of Leling, stationed him at Yanci, and put his son Shao Yi in charge as chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 續綏懷流散，多歸附之。

translations.literal: Shao Xu comforted and gathered scattered refugees, and many attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: He sheltered displaced people, and a great many rallied to his banner.

sentences.zh: 石勒既破浚，遣乂還招續，續以孤危無援，權附於勒，勒亦以乂為督護。

translations.literal: After Shi Le had defeated Wang Jun, he sent Shao Yi back to summon Shao Xu; Shao Xu, isolated and without aid, submitted provisionally to Shi Le, and Shi Le likewise appointed Shao Yi chief of staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Le had broken Wang Jun, he sent Shao Yi back to win his father over; isolated and without allies, Shao Xu submitted for the moment to Shi Le, who again named Shao Yi chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 既而段匹磾在薊，遺書要續俱歸元帝，續從之。

translations.literal: Not long after, Duan Pidi was at Ji; he sent a letter inviting Shao Xu to return together to Emperor Yuan, and Shao Xu followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Duan Pidi, holding Ji, wrote urging Shao Xu to come south with him to Emperor Yuan, and Shao Xu agreed.

sentences.zh: 其下諫曰：「今棄勒歸匹磾，任子危矣。

translations.literal: His subordinates remonstrated: "If we now abandon Shi Le for Duan Pidi, the hostage son will be in peril.
translations.idiomatic: His officers warned him: "Turn from Shi Le to Duan Pidi and the son you left as hostage is lost.

sentences.zh: 」續垂泣曰：「我出身為國，豈得顧子而為叛臣哉！

translations.literal: Shao Xu wept and said: "I left home to serve the state—how could I care for my son and become a traitor!
translations.idiomatic: Shao Xu wept and said, "I entered public life for the dynasty—am I to save my boy and turn traitor?

sentences.zh: 」遂絕於勒，勒乃害乂。

translations.literal: Thereupon he broke with Shi Le, whereupon Shi Le had Shao Yi killed.
translations.idiomatic: He broke with Shi Le; Shi Le then executed Shao Yi.

sentences.zh: 續懼勒攻，先求救於匹磾，匹磾遣弟文鴦救續。

translations.literal: Shao Xu feared an attack by Shi Le and first begged help from Duan Pidi; Pidi sent his younger brother Duan Wenying to relieve Shao Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Shi Le's assault, he appealed first to Duan Pidi, who sent his brother Wenying to his rescue.

sentences.zh: 文鴦未至，勒已率八千騎圍續。

translations.literal: Before Wenying had arrived, Shi Le had already led eight thousand horsemen to besiege Shao Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le reached him first with eight thousand cavalry and threw a ring around his position.

sentences.zh: 勒素畏鮮卑，又聞文鴦至，乃棄攻具東走。

translations.literal: Shi Le had always feared the Xianbei, and when he heard Wenying was coming he abandoned his siege equipment and fled east.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le had always dreaded the Xianbei; at word of Wenying's approach he abandoned his engines and bolted east.

sentences.zh: 續與文鴦追勒至安陵，不及，虜勒所署官，並驅三千餘家，又遣騎入抄勒北邊，掠常山，亦二千家而還。

translations.literal: Shao Xu and Wenying pursued Shi Le to Anling but did not overtake him; they captured Shi Le's appointed officials, drove off more than three thousand households, also sent cavalry to raid Shi Le's northern border, plundered Changshan, and likewise returned with two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Xu and Wenying chased him to Anling but could not catch him; they took the officials Shi Le had installed, marched off over three thousand families, sent riders to scour his northern marches and sack Changshan, and came back with two thousand more households besides.

sentences.zh: 匹磾既殺劉琨，夷晉多怨叛，遂率其徒依續。

translations.literal: After Duan Pidi had killed Liu Kun, Chinese and tribesmen for the most part resented him and rebelled; he therefore led his followers to rely on Shao Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Once Duan Pidi had murdered Liu Kun, many Chinese and tribal followers turned against him, so he brought his host to Shao Xu's side.

sentences.zh: 勒南和令趙領等率廣川、渤海千餘家背勒歸續。

translations.literal: Zhao Ling, magistrate of Nanhe under Shi Le, led more than a thousand households from Guangchuan and Bohai to betray Shi Le and join Shao Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ling of Nanhe, serving under Shi Le, led over a thousand families from Guangchuan and Bohai to defect to Shao Xu.

sentences.zh: 而帝以續為平原樂安太守、右將軍、冀州刺史，進平北將軍、假節，封祝阿子。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Shao Xu prefect of Pingyuan and Le'an, General of the Right, and inspector of Ji province, advanced him to General Who Pacifies the North with credential, and enfeoffed him as viscount of Zhu'e.
translations.idiomatic: The court named him prefect of Pingyuan and Le'an, General of the Right, and inspector of Ji, then promoted him to General Who Pacifies the North with baton of authority and created him viscount of Zhu'e.

sentences.zh: 續遣兄子武邑內史存與文鴦率匹磾眾就食平原，為石季龍所破。

translations.literal: Shao Xu sent his nephew Cun, interior governor of Wuyi, and Wenying to lead Pidi's followers to forage in Pingyuan; they were defeated by Shi Jilong.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched his nephew Cun, Wuyi's interior governor, with Wenying to escort Pidi's people into Pingyuan for supplies; Shi Hu shattered their force.

sentences.zh: 續先與曹嶷互相侵掠，嶷因存等敗，乃破續屯田，又抄其戶口，續首尾相救，疲於奔命。

translations.literal: Shao Xu had earlier raided back and forth with Cao Yi; Yi because Cun and the others were defeated then smashed Shao Xu's military colonies and plundered his registered households; Shao Xu rescued head and tail in turn and was exhausted running from crisis to crisis.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Xu and Cao Yi had long raided one another; after Cun's defeat Yi overran his military farms and seized his people, leaving Shao Xu racing from front to rear until he was worn threadbare.

sentences.zh: 太興初，續遣存及文鴦屯濟南黃巾固，因以逼嶷，嶷懼，求和。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taixing, Shao Xu sent Cun and Wenying to garrison the Yellow Turban fort at Jinan in order to pressure Cao Yi; Yi feared and sued for peace.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taixing era he sent Cun and Wenying to hold the old Yellow Turban stronghold at Jinan and squeeze Cao Yi until Yi sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 俄而匹磾率眾攻段末杯，石勒知續孤危，遣季龍乘虛圍續。

translations.literal: Soon Pidi led his host to attack Duan Mobo; Shi Le, knowing Shao Xu was isolated and imperiled, sent Shi Jilong to exploit the void and besiege Shao Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Then Pidi marched against Duan Mobo; Shi Le, seeing Shao Xu left exposed, sent Shi Hu to fall on him while his guard was down.

sentences.zh: 季龍騎至城下，掠其居人，續率眾出救，季龍伏騎斷其後，遂為季龍所得，使續降其城。

translations.literal: Shi Jilong's cavalry reached the foot of the city, plundered its inhabitants; Shao Xu led his host out to rescue them; Shi Jilong ambushed cavalry and cut off his rear; thereupon he was taken by Shi Jilong; he had Shao Xu persuade the city to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu rode to the walls and dragged off the townsfolk; Shao Xu sortied to save them, but Hu's hidden horse cut his retreat and took him prisoner, then ordered him to talk the garrison down.

sentences.zh: 續呼其兄子竺等曰：「吾志雪國難，以報所受，不幸至此。

translations.literal: Shao Xu called to his elder brother's sons Zhu and the others: "My will was to wipe away the state's shame and repay what I received; unluckily I have reached this point.
translations.idiomatic: He called his nephews Zhu and the rest: "I meant to clear the throne's disgrace and repay every favor the court showed me; fate has brought me here instead.

sentences.zh: 汝等努力自勉，便奉匹磾為主，勿有二心。」

translations.literal: You must strive with all your strength, then acknowledge Pidi as lord—do not harbor a second heart."
translations.idiomatic: Bear up, every one of you, take Duan Pidi as your chief, and never divide your loyalty."

sentences.zh: 時帝既聞續沒，下詔曰：「邵續忠烈在公，義誠慷慨，綏集荒餘，憂國亡身。

translations.literal: When the emperor had heard that Shao Xu was lost, he issued an edict: "Shao Xu's loyalty and fierce integrity were for the public good; in righteousness he was fervent; he gathered the scattered survivors of the wilderness and gave his body for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of Shao Xu's fall, the emperor promulgated an edict: "Shao Xu served the realm with blazing loyalty; his sense of duty ran high; he gathered the broken remnants of the north and gave his life for the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 功勳未遂，不幸陷沒，朕用悼恨於懷。

translations.literal: Merit and enterprise were not yet completed when he was engulfed in disaster; I therefore harbor grief and regret in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: His work was unfinished when disaster swallowed him; I carry sorrow and regret in my breast.

sentences.zh: 所統任重，宜時有代。

translations.literal: The command he bore was weighty and should at this time have a successor.
translations.idiomatic: The post he held was too grave to stand empty; a successor must be named at once.

sentences.zh: 其部曲文武，已共推其息緝為營主。

translations.literal: The civil and military officers of his army corps have jointly recommended his son Ji as camp commander.
translations.idiomatic: His staff and troops have together raised his son Ji to lead the camp.

sentences.zh: 續之忠誠，著於公私，今立其子，足以安眾，一以續本位即授緝，使總率所統，效節國難，雪其家仇。」

translations.literal: Shao Xu's loyalty has been manifest in public and private alike; now that we establish his son, it should be enough to reassure the host—in one act grant him Shao Xu's former rank and invest Ji, that he may command all who followed his father, devote his strength to the state's crisis, and avenge his family's wrongs."
translations.idiomatic: His faithfulness shone at court and in the ranks alike; naming his heir will steady the army—invest Ji with every title his father held, let him lead the old command, serve the throne through this ordeal, and wipe away the family's blood-debt."

sentences.zh: 季龍遣使送續於勒，勒使使徐光讓之曰：「國家應符撥亂，八表宅心，遺晉怖威，遠竄揚越。

translations.literal: Shi Jilong sent Shao Xu under escort to Shi Le; Shi Le ordered his envoy Xu Guang to reproach him: "The state bears the tally and quells chaos; the eight quarters nestle at our heart; the remnant Jin fear our might and flee far to Yang and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu sent Shao Xu to Shi Le, who had Xu Guang rebuke him: "Our house holds the mandate and stills turmoil; the world turns to us; the rump Jin tremble and scatter toward the Yangzi and the south.

sentences.zh: 而續蟻封海阿，跋扈王命，以夷狄不足為君邪？

translations.literal: Yet you, Shao Xu, are like ants sealing a mound beside the sea, arrogant toward the king's command—do you hold that barbarians are unworthy to be lords?
translations.idiomatic: Yet you crouch like ants on a coastal hillock and flout the Son of Heaven—do you imagine that we barbarians are unfit to rule?

sentences.zh: 何無上之甚也！

translations.literal: How extreme is your lack of respect for what is above!
translations.idiomatic: Never have I seen such contempt for authority!

sentences.zh: 國有常刑，于分甘乎？

translations.literal: The state has its constant punishments—as for the lot assigned you, are you content with it?
translations.idiomatic: The law has its fixed penalties; will you go to your fate willingly?

sentences.zh: 」續對曰：「晉末饑亂，奔控無所，保合鄉宗，庶全老幼。

translations.literal: Shao Xu replied: "In the Jin's final years there was famine and chaos; there was nowhere to flee; I banded with my townspeople hoping to preserve the old and young in full.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Xu answered: "When the Jin collapsed in famine and riot there was nowhere to run; I drew my clansmen together only to keep the old and the young alive.

sentences.zh: 屬大王龍飛之始，委命納質，精誠無感，不蒙慈恕。

translations.literal: When the Great King first rose like a dragon I placed my life in your hands and sent hostages; my earnest devotion aroused no response—I was not favored with merciful forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: At your first rising I offered my life and sent hostages; my good faith never moved you, and I was shown no mercy.

sentences.zh: 言歸遺晉，仍荷寵授，誓盡忠節，實無二心。

translations.literal: When I returned to the remnant Jin I still received thick honors; I swore to exhaust loyalty to the utmost—I truly had no second heart.
translations.idiomatic: When I went back to the Jin they heaped rank on me; I swore the fullest loyalty and never wavered inwardly.

sentences.zh: 且受彼厚榮，而復二三其趣者，恐亦不容于明朝矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, one who took such thick honors from them and then shifted his purpose this way and that would hardly be tolerated by a luminous court either.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, a man who took their lavish favors and then tacked with every wind would find no room even in a clear-sighted court.

sentences.zh: 周文生於東夷，大禹出於西羌，帝王之興，蓋惟天命所屬，德之所招，當何常邪！

translations.literal: King Wen of the Zhou was born among the Eastern Yi; the Great Yu came from the Western Qiang—the rise of emperors and kings is surely whatever Heaven assigns and virtue summons; how can there be one constant rule!
translations.idiomatic: King Wen sprang from the eastern Yi, Great Yu from the western Qiang—dynasties rise where Heaven places them and virtue calls; what single rule could bind them?

sentences.zh: 伏惟大王聖武自天，道隆虞夏，凡在含生，孰不延首神化，恥隔皇風，而況囚乎！

translations.literal: Humbly I reflect: the Great King's sacred martial prowess comes from Heaven; his way towers above Yu and Xia—among everything that draws breath, who would not crane toward divine transformation and blush to be shut off from your royal airs—how much more a captive like myself!
translations.idiomatic: I dare say your sacred might is heaven-sent and your virtue outshines Yu and Xia—every living soul longs for your transforming rule and is ashamed to stand outside your breeze—how much more a prisoner in your hands!

sentences.zh: 使囚去真即偽，不得早叩天門者，大王負囚，囚不負大王也。

translations.literal: If you make me leave the true for the false and keep me from knocking early at Heaven's gate, the Great King will have wronged this captive—this captive will not have wronged the Great King.
translations.idiomatic: Should you force me from truth into treachery and bar me from serving the rightful court, the fault will be yours, Great King, not mine.

sentences.zh: 釁鼓之刑，囚之恆分，但恨天實為之，謂之何哉！

translations.literal: The punishment of smearing blood on the war drum is the captive's constant lot; I only regret that Heaven brought it about—what can one say!
translations.idiomatic: Death on the drum is what any prisoner expects; I only grieve that Heaven willed it so—what more is there to say?

sentences.zh: 」勒曰：「其言慨至，孤愧之多矣。

translations.literal: Shi Le said: "His words are fervent to the utmost; I am much ashamed before him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le said, "He speaks from the depths; I am ashamed before him.

sentences.zh: 夫忠於其君者，乃吾所求也。

translations.literal: One who is loyal to his lord is exactly what I seek."
translations.idiomatic: A man loyal to his sovereign is the very thing I prize."

sentences.zh: 」命張寶延之於館，厚撫之，尋以為從事中郎。

translations.literal: He ordered Zhang Bao to extend him in a guest house, treated him generously, and soon appointed him retainer clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He told Zhang Bao to lodge him with honor, showered him with gifts, and soon named him palace retainer.

sentences.zh: 今自後諸克敵擒俊，皆送之，不得輒害，冀獲如續之流。

translations.literal: From now on whenever you crush the foe and seize outstanding captives, send them here alive—do not kill them at will; I hope to obtain more men in Shao Xu's mold.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth every time you break an enemy and seize a noted leader, bring him here alive—never kill such men on your own; I want more captives with Shao Xu's mettle.

sentences.zh: 初，季龍之攻續也，朝廷有王敦之逼，不遑救恤。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shi Jilong had attacked Shao Xu, the court was pressed by Wang Dun and had no leisure to send relief.
translations.idiomatic: While Shi Hu besieged Shao Xu, the court was pinned by Wang Dun and could spare no rescue.

sentences.zh: 續既為勒所執，身灌園鬻菜，以供衣食。

translations.literal: After Shao Xu was taken by Shi Le, he personally watered gardens and sold vegetables to supply clothing and food.
translations.idiomatic: Once in Shi Le's hands he tended gardens and peddled greens with his own hands to earn his keep.

sentences.zh: 勒屢遣察之，歎曰；

translations.literal: Shi Le repeatedly sent men to observe him and sighed, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le sent watchers again and again, then sighed and said:

sentences.zh: 「此真高人矣。

translations.literal: "This is truly a man set above the common run.
translations.idiomatic: "Here is a man who stands apart from the crowd.

sentences.zh: 不如是，安足貴乎！

translations.literal: Were it not so, how would he be worthy of esteem!"
translations.idiomatic: Were it otherwise he would not be worth honoring at all!"

sentences.zh: 」嘉其清苦，數賜穀帛。

translations.literal: He praised his austerity and several times bestowed grain and silk.
translations.idiomatic: He admired his austerity and sent grain and cloth time after time.

sentences.zh: 每臨朝嗟歎，以勵群官。

translations.literal: Whenever he faced court he sighed with praise to encourage the host of officials.
translations.idiomatic: At every audience he praised Shao Xu aloud to steel his ministers.

sentences.zh: 續被獲之後，存及竺、緝等與匹磾嬰城距寇，而帝又假存揚武將軍、武邑太守。

translations.literal: After Shao Xu was captured, Cun along with Zhu, Ji, and the others, with Pidi, sealed the city against the invaders; the emperor concurrently appointed Cun General Who Rouses Valor and prefect of Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: After Shao Xu fell, Cun, Zhu, Ji, and the rest held the walls with Duan Pidi against the foe while the court named Cun General Who Rouses Valor and prefect of Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 勒屢遣季龍攻之，戰守疲苦，不能自立。

translations.literal: Shi Le repeatedly sent Shi Jilong to attack them; battle and defense wore them down until they could not establish themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le hurled Shi Hu against them again and again until attack and defense alike broke their strength.

sentences.zh: 久之，匹磾及其弟文鴦與竺、緝等悉見獲，惟存得潰圍南奔，在道為賊所殺。

translations.literal: After a long time Pidi and his younger brother Wenying with Zhu, Ji, and the others were all captured; only Cun broke out of the encirclement and fled south, but on the road was killed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In time Pidi, Wenying, Zhu, and Ji were all taken; only Cun burst the ring and ran south, only to die at bandit hands on the road.

sentences.zh: 續竟亦遇害。

translations.literal: Shao Xu in the end was likewise killed.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Xu too was put to death in the end.

sentences.zh: 李矩

translations.literal: Li Ju
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju

sentences.zh: 李矩，字世回，平陽人也。

translations.literal: Li Ju, style name Shihui, was a man of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju, courtesy Shihui, came from Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 童齔時，與群兒聚戲，便為其率，計畫指授，有成人之量。

translations.literal: In childhood when he gathered with other children to play, he became their leader, planning and directing as would an adult.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy, when he played with neighborhood children he always commanded them, laying plans like a grown man.

sentences.zh: 及長，為吏，送故縣令于長安，征西將軍梁王肜以為牙門。

translations.literal: When grown he became a clerk; seeing off a former magistrate to Chang'an, the western expedition general Sima Rong, Prince of Liang, took him on as yamen guard.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he served as a clerk; escorting a former magistrate to Chang'an, he was recruited as a gate guard by Sima Rong, Prince of Liang, the general commanding the western expedition.

sentences.zh: 伐氐齊萬年有殊功，封東明亭侯。

translations.literal: In the campaign against the Di rebel Qi Wannian he had exceptional merit and was enfeoffed as village marquis of Dongming.
translations.idiomatic: He won outstanding distinction against the Di rebel Qi Wannian and was created village marquis of Dongming.

sentences.zh: 還為本郡督護。

translations.literal: On his return he was chief of staff for his native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Back home he became chief of staff of his commandery.

sentences.zh: 太守宋胄欲以所親吳畿代之，矩謝病去。

translations.literal: The prefect Song Zhou wished to replace him with his intimate Wu Ji; Li Ju pleaded illness and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Song Zhou meant to swap him for a favorite, Wu Ji; Li Ju pleaded illness and stepped down.

sentences.zh: 畿恐矩復還，陰使人刺矩，會有人救之，故得免。

translations.literal: Wu Ji feared Li Ju might return and secretly sent someone to stab Li Ju; someone rescued him, therefore he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ji dreaded his return and hired an assassin; a passerby saved him and he lived.

sentences.zh: 屬劉元海攻平陽，百姓奔走，矩素為鄉人所愛，乃推為塢主，東屯滎陽，後移新鄭。

translations.literal: When Liu Yuan attacked Pingyang and the common people fled in panic, Li Ju was loved by his townspeople and was pushed to be fortress chief; he encamped east at Xingyang and later moved to Xinzheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yuan stormed Pingyang and the people scattered, the locals, who loved Li Ju, made him chief of their fort; he moved east to Xingyang and later shifted to Xinzheng.

sentences.zh: 矩勇毅多權略，志在立功，東海王越以為汝陰太守。

translations.literal: Li Ju was brave and resolute and full of stratagems; his aim was set on achievement; Prince Donghai Sima Yue appointed him prefect of Ruyin.
translations.idiomatic: Bold, resolute, and full of schemes, he burned to make his mark; Prince Donghai, Sima Yue, named him prefect of Ruyin.

sentences.zh: 永嘉初，使矩與汝南太守袁孚率眾修洛陽千金堨，以利運漕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongjia the court had Li Ju and the prefect of Runan, Yuan Fu, lead their forces to repair the Qianjin weir at Luoyang to benefit transport by canal.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongjia reign he and Yuan Fu, prefect of Runan, were ordered to restore Luoyang's Qianjin weir for the grain boats.

sentences.zh: 及洛陽不守，太尉荀籓奔陽城，衛將軍華薈奔成皋。

translations.literal: When Luoyang did not hold, grand commandant Xun Fan fled to Yangcheng and guard general Hua Hui fled to Chenggao.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang fell, grand commandant Xun Fan ran to Yangcheng and guard general Hua Hui to Chenggao.

sentences.zh: 時大饑，賊帥侯都等每略人而食之，籓、薈部曲多為所啖。

translations.literal: At that time there was great famine; the bandit chieftain Hou Du and others repeatedly seized people and ate them; many of Fan's and Hui's retainers were devoured.
translations.idiomatic: Famine stalked the land; the outlaw Hou Du and his gang seized people for food, and many of Xun Fan's and Hua Hui's followers were eaten.

sentences.zh: 矩討都等滅之，乃營護籓、薈，各為立屋宇，輸穀以給之。

translations.literal: Li Ju campaigned against Hou Du and destroyed them, then protected Fan and Hui, for each building houses and shipping grain to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju destroyed Hou Du, then sheltered Fan and Hui, building houses for both and sending grain to keep them fed.

sentences.zh: 及籓承制，建行臺，假矩滎陽太守。

translations.literal: When Fan assumed plenipotentiary command and set up a mobile headquarters, he provisionally named Li Ju prefect of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun Fan took acting authority and raised a field headquarters, he named Li Ju provisional prefect of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 矩招懷離散，遠近多附之。

translations.literal: Li Ju summoned and comforted the scattered; near and far largely attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: He called in the displaced and won over people from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 石勒親率大眾襲矩，矩遣老弱入山，令所在散牛馬，因設伏以待之。

translations.literal: Shi Le personally led a great host against Li Ju; Li Ju sent the old and weak into the mountains and had people everywhere loose oxen and horses, then set an ambush to await him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le marched in person against him; Li Ju sent the noncombatants into the hills, turned cattle and horses loose across the countryside, and laid a trap.

sentences.zh: 賊爭取牛馬。

translations.literal: The bandits vied to seize the oxen and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le's men scrambled to round up the livestock.

sentences.zh: 伏發，齊呼，聲動山谷，遂大破之，斬獲甚眾，勒乃退。

translations.literal: The ambush rose; they shouted in unison; the sound shook the valleys; thereupon they greatly defeated him, killing and capturing very many, and Shi Le withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The ambush sprang; a single roar shook the valleys; Li Ju shattered the army with heavy slaughter and drove Shi Le back.

sentences.zh: 籓表元帝，加矩冠軍將軍，軺車幢蓋，進封陽武縣侯，領河東、平陽太守。

translations.literal: Xun Fan presented Li Ju to Emperor Yuan, who added to Li Ju the titles General Who Crowns the Army, light chariot with canopy, advanced his fief to county marquis of Yangwu, and had him hold the offices of prefect of Hedong and Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Fan recommended him to Emperor Yuan, who added General Who Crowns the Army, a light chariot with canopy, raised his fief to county marquis of Yangwu, and let him serve jointly as prefect of Hedong and Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 時饑饉相仍，又多疫癘，矩垂心撫恤，百姓賴焉。

translations.literal: At that time famine followed famine and pestilence spread; Li Ju lavished care on relief and comfort, and the people relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Famine and plague ran together; Li Ju poured his energy into relief, and the people clung to him.

sentences.zh: 會長安群盜東下，所在多虜掠，矩遣部將擊破之，盡得賊所略婦女千餘人。

translations.literal: It happened that bandits from Chang'an moved east, plundering wherever they went; Li Ju sent a subordinate general to break them and fully obtained the more than a thousand women the bandits had seized.
translations.idiomatic: When eastern raiders from Chang'an swept through the region, he sent a deputy to crush them and recovered over a thousand women they had taken.

sentences.zh: 諸將以非矩所部。

translations.literal: The generals held that they were not under Li Ju's command.
translations.idiomatic: His officers argued that these captives were not from his own command.

sentences.zh: 欲遂留之。

translations.literal: They wished to detain them.
translations.idiomatic: They wanted to keep the women for themselves.

sentences.zh: 矩曰：「俱是國家臣妾，焉有此彼此！

translations.literal: Li Ju said: "They are all alike subjects of the state—how can there be this distinction of yours and mine!
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju said, "They are all the emperor's people—how can we draw a line between his household and mine?

sentences.zh: 」乃一時遣之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent them off all at once.
translations.idiomatic: He sent every one of them home together.

sentences.zh: 時劉琨所假河內太守郭默為劉元海所逼，乞歸於矩，矩將使其甥郭誦迎致之，而不敢進。

translations.literal: At that time Guo Mo, whom Liu Kun had provisionally appointed prefect of Henan, was pressed by Liu Yuan and begged to return to Li Ju; Li Ju was about to have his nephew Guo Song go welcome him but did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Mo, Liu Kun's acting prefect of Henan, was harried by Liu Yuan and begged Li Ju for refuge; Li Ju meant to send his nephew Guo Song to escort him in, but Song hesitated to move.

sentences.zh: 會劉琨遣參軍張肇，率鮮卑範勝等五百餘騎往長安，屬默被圍，道路不通，將還依邵續，行至矩營，矩謂肇曰：「默是劉公所授，公家之事，知無不為。

translations.literal: It happened that Liu Kun sent adjutant Zhang Zhao leading more than five hundred Xianbei riders under Fan Sheng and others toward Chang'an; because Guo Mo was besieged the roads were not open; they were about to return and rely on Shao Xu; when they reached Li Ju's camp, Li Ju said to Zhang Zhao: "Guo Mo was appointed by Lord Liu; in matters of your master's house, I know there is nothing I would not do.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Liu Kun dispatched Zhang Zhao with over five hundred Xianbei horse under Fan Sheng toward Chang'an; blocked by the siege of Guo Mo, they turned back toward Shao Xu and halted at Li Ju's camp. Li Ju told Zhang Zhao, "Guo Mo holds Liu Kun's commission; whatever serves your patron's interest, I will do."

sentences.zh: 」屠各舊畏鮮卑，遂邀肇為聲援，肇許之。

translations.literal: The Tuge of old feared the Xianbei; they therefore intercepted Zhang Zhao to request his support as a diversion, and Zhao consented.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuge had always dreaded Xianbei horse, so they waylaid Zhang Zhao and begged him to show a banner of support; Zhao agreed.

sentences.zh: 賊望見鮮卑，不戰而走。

translations.literal: The bandits, seeing the Xianbei, fled without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: The besiegers sighted the Xianbei and bolted without offering battle.

sentences.zh: 誦潛遣輕舟濟河，使勇士夜襲懷城，掩賊留營，又大破之。

translations.literal: Guo Song secretly sent light boats across the Yellow River and bold men to raid Huai city by night, surprise the bandit camp left behind, and again greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Song slipped light boats across the river and sent picked men to storm Huai by night, falling on the enemy rear camp and routing them again.

sentences.zh: 默遂率其屬歸於矩。

translations.literal: Guo Mo thereupon led his following to submit to Li Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Mo then brought his command to Li Ju.

sentences.zh: 後劉聰遣從弟暢步騎三萬討矩，屯于韓王故壘，相去七里，遣使招矩。

translations.literal: Later Liu Cong sent his cousin Liu Chang with thirty thousand foot and horse to campaign against Li Ju, encamping at the old rampart of Han Wang seven li away, and sent a messenger to summon Li Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liu Cong dispatched his cousin Liu Chang with thirty thousand foot and horse against Li Ju, pitching camp on Han Wang's old fort seven li off, and sent a herald to call Li Ju in.

sentences.zh: 時暢卒至，矩未暇為備，遣使奉牛酒詐降於暢，潛匿精勇，見其老弱。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Chang had arrived suddenly; Li Ju had no time to prepare; he sent envoys bearing oxen and wine feigning surrender to Liu Chang while hiding picked warriors and showing him only the old and weak.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chang came on too fast for Li Ju to ready a defense, so he sent oxen and wine as a sham surrender while hiding his veterans and parading only the aged and feeble.

sentences.zh: 暢不以為虞，大饗渠帥，人皆醉飽。

translations.literal: Liu Chang took no precautions, feasted his chieftains grandly, and everyone was drunk and full.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chang dropped his guard, threw a great feast for his chiefs, and they all drank themselves full.

sentences.zh: 矩謀夜襲之，兵士以賊眾，皆有懼色。

translations.literal: Li Ju planned a night raid; his soldiers, seeing the enemy's numbers, all showed fear on their faces.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju meant to strike by night, but his men blanched at the size of the enemy host.

sentences.zh: 矩令郭誦禱鄭子產祠曰：「君昔相鄭，惡鳥不鳴。

translations.literal: Li Ju ordered Guo Song to pray at the shrine of Zichan of Zheng: "You once served Zheng as minister—even ill-omened birds did not cry.
translations.idiomatic: He told Guo Song to pray at Zichan of Zheng's temple: "When you ruled Zheng, ill-omened birds fell silent.

sentences.zh: 凶胡臭羯，何得過庭！

translations.literal: How can foul barbarians and stinking Jie cross this courtyard!
translations.idiomatic: What business have murderous Hu and reeking Jie in this court!

sentences.zh: 」使巫揚言：「東裏有教，當遣神兵相助。

translations.literal: He had shamans proclaim loudly: "The god of the eastern quarter has issued a command—divine soldiers are to be sent to aid us.
translations.idiomatic: He set shamans to cry abroad: "The eastern god has spoken—heaven will send warriors to our aid.

sentences.zh: 」將士聞之，皆踴躍爭進。

translations.literal: When officers and men heard this, all leaped up vying to advance.
translations.idiomatic: The troops heard it and surged forward, each man eager to be first.

sentences.zh: 乃使誦及督護楊璋等選勇敢千人，夜掩暢營，獲鎧馬甚多，斬首數千級，暢僅以身免。

translations.literal: He then had Guo Song and chief of staff Yang Zhang and others pick a thousand brave men and strike Liu Chang's camp by night; they seized very many armored horses and cut off several thousand heads; Chang barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Guo Song with Yang Zhang and other picked men—one thousand bold fighters—to fall on Chang's camp at night. They took stacks of armored horses, heaped up thousands of heads, and Chang alone slipped away alive.

sentences.zh: 先是，郭默聞矩被攻，遣弟芝率眾援之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Guo Mo heard Li Ju was under attack, he sent his younger brother Zhi with a host to aid him.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, Guo Mo had learned that Li Ju was pressed and dispatched his brother Zhi with troops to help.

sentences.zh: 既而聞破暢，芝復馳來赴矩。

translations.literal: Afterward, hearing Chang had been defeated, Zhi again galloped to join Li Ju.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Chang was broken, Zhi raced back to Li Ju's side.

sentences.zh: 矩乃與芝馬五百匹，分軍為三道，夜追賊，復大獲而旋。

translations.literal: Li Ju thereupon gave Zhi five hundred horses, divided the army into three columns, pursued the bandits by night, and again took a great haul before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju handed Zhi five hundred horses, split his force into three night columns, ran the enemy down, and came home laden with spoil.

sentences.zh: 先是，聰使其將趙固鎮洛陽，長史周振與固不協，密陳固罪。

translations.literal: Earlier, Liu Cong had sent his general Zhao Gu to garrison Luoyang; chief clerk Zhou Zhen was at odds with Gu and secretly reported Gu's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liu Cong had posted Zhao Gu at Luoyang; Zhou Zhen, Gu's chief of staff, hated him and denounced him in secret to the throne.

sentences.zh: 矩之破暢也，帳中得聰書，敕暢平矩訖，過洛陽，收固斬之，便以振代固。

translations.literal: When Li Ju defeated Chang, in the tent he obtained a letter from Liu Cong instructing Chang, once Li Ju was pacified, to pass through Luoyang, seize Gu and execute him, and then replace Gu with Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the rout of Liu Chang, Li Ju captured an order from Liu Cong telling Chang to finish off Li Ju, then swing through Luoyang, arrest Zhao Gu, put him to death, and install Zhou Zhen in his place.

sentences.zh: 矩送以示固，固即斬振父子，遂率騎一千來降，矩還令守洛。

translations.literal: Li Ju sent it to show Gu; Gu immediately executed Zhen and his sons, then led a thousand horsemen to surrender; Li Ju ordered him back to hold Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju forwarded the letter to Zhao Gu, who at once beheaded Zhou Zhen and his sons, rode in with a thousand horse to defect, and was sent back to guard Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 後數月，聰遣其太子粲率劉雅生等步騎十萬屯孟津北岸，分遣雅生攻趙固於洛。

translations.literal: Several months later Liu Cong sent his heir Liu Can with Liu Yasheng and others, one hundred thousand foot and horse, to encamp on the north bank of the Meng ford, and separately sent Yasheng to attack Zhao Gu at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Months later Liu Cong dispatched the crown prince Liu Can with Liu Yasheng and a host of one hundred thousand to the north shore at Mengjin, while Yasheng was sent to strike Zhao Gu in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 固奔陽城山，遣弟告急，矩遣郭誦屯洛口以救之。

translations.literal: Gu fled to Mount Yangcheng and sent his younger brother with an urgent plea; Li Ju sent Guo Song to hold the mouth of the Luo to relieve him.
translations.idiomatic: Gu bolted to Yangcheng Mountain and begged for help; Li Ju stationed Guo Song at the Luo estuary to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 誦使將張皮簡精卒千人夜渡河。

translations.literal: Song had his general Zhang Pi pick a thousand picked troops and cross the river by night.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Song told Zhang Pi to take a thousand elite men across the Yellow River under cover of dark.

sentences.zh: 粲候者告有兵至，粲恃其眾，不以為虞。

translations.literal: Can's scouts reported troops approaching; Can relied on his numbers and took no precautions.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can's pickets reported an approaching force, but he trusted his mass of men and never tightened his guard.

sentences.zh: 既而誦等奄至，十道俱攻，粲眾驚擾，一時奔潰，殺傷太半，因據其營，獲其器械軍資不可勝數。

translations.literal: Soon Song and the others arrived suddenly; they attacked on ten fronts at once; Can's host was thrown into panic and fled in rout at one stroke; more than half were killed or wounded; they therefore occupied his camp and captured weapons and military stores beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Then Guo Song struck from nowhere along ten fronts at once. Liu Can's army panicked and stampeded; over half were cut down. Song seized the camp and cartloads of arms and supplies beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 及旦，粲見皮等人少，更與雅生悉餘眾攻之，苦戰二十餘日不能下。

translations.literal: At dawn Can saw Pi and the others were few in number and again with Yasheng led all remaining troops against them; they fought bitterly more than twenty days but could not take them.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak Liu Can saw how few Zhang Pi's men were and threw every survivor, with Yasheng, into a siege that ground on for twenty days without success.

sentences.zh: 矩進救之，使壯士三千泛舟迎皮。

translations.literal: Li Ju advanced to relieve them and sent three thousand stalwarts in boats to meet Pi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju marched to the rescue and floated three thousand picked men downriver to lift Zhang Pi out.

sentences.zh: 賊臨河列陣，作長鉤以鉤船，連戰數日不得渡。

translations.literal: The bandits lined up along the river and fashioned long hooks to snag the boats; they fought several days and could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy drew up along the bank and rigged long hooks to snare the boats; day after day of fighting still left Li Ju's men unable to cross.

sentences.zh: 矩夜遣部將格增潛濟入皮壘，與皮選精騎千餘，而殺所獲牛馬，焚燒器械，夜穴圍而出，奔武牢。

translations.literal: Li Ju by night sent subordinate general Ge Zeng to slip across and enter Pi's fort; with Pi he chose more than a thousand picked horsemen, then slaughtered the captured oxen and horses, burned the equipment, dug through the encirclement by night, broke out, and fled to Wulao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju sent Ge Zeng by night to ford into Zhang Pi's ring; together they took a thousand crack horsemen, slaughtered the draft animals, torched their gear, burrowed through the lines after dark, and broke for Wulao.

sentences.zh: 聰追之，不及而退。

translations.literal: Liu Cong pursued them, did not overtake them, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong gave chase but could not catch them and turned back.

sentences.zh: 聰因憤恚，發病而死。

translations.literal: Liu Cong thereupon, in rage and resentment, fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong sickened with fury and died of it.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其功，除矩都督河南三郡軍事、安西將軍、滎陽太守，封修武縣侯。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his merit, appointed Li Ju supervisor of military affairs for the three Henan commanderies, General Who Pacifies the West, and prefect of Xingyang, and enfeoffed him as marquis of Xiuwu county.
translations.idiomatic: The court commended him, named him area commander for the three Henan commanderies with the titles General Who Pacifies the West and prefect of Xingyang, and created him marquis of Xiuwu.

sentences.zh: 及劉粲嗣位，昏虐日甚，其將靳准乃起兵殺粲，並其宗族，發聰塚，斬其屍，遣使歸矩，稱「劉元海屠各小丑，因大晉事故之際，作亂幽并，矯稱天命，至令二帝幽沒虜庭。

translations.literal: When Liu Can succeeded to the throne, his debauchery and cruelty grew daily; his general Jin Zhun thereupon raised troops, killed Can together with his whole clan, opened Liu Cong's tomb, hacked his corpse, and sent a messenger to Li Ju saying: "Liu Yuan of the Tuge was a petty bandit who, exploiting the Jin's misfortune, made trouble in You and Bing and falsely claimed Heaven's mandate, with the result that the two emperors languish captive in the barbarian court,
translations.idiomatic: Under Liu Can the throne turned ever more vicious and depraved until Jin Zhun mutinied, slaughtered Can and his kin, rifled Liu Cong's grave, mutilated the dead emperor's body, and wrote Li Ju that "Liu Yuan, that Tuge chieftain, used the Jin's collapse to riot through You and Bing while pretending to a mandate, leaving both our emperors rotting in alien hands,

sentences.zh: 輒率眾扶侍梓宮，因請上聞」。

translations.literal: I have led the host to escort the imperial coffins and therefore request that this be reported above."
translations.idiomatic: and I now march the army to escort the late emperors' catafalques and beg you to lay this before the Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 矩馳表於帝，帝遣太常韓胤等奉迎梓宮，未至而准已為石勒、劉曜所沒。

translations.literal: Li Ju galloped a memorial to the emperor; the emperor sent grand master of ceremonies Han Yin and others to welcome the coffins, but before they arrived Zhun had already been destroyed by Shi Le and Liu Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju sent a flying memorial; the court dispatched Han Yin and others to meet the hearses, but before they arrived Jin Zhun had been crushed by Shi Le and Liu Yao.

sentences.zh: 矩以眾少不足立功，每慷慨憤歎。

translations.literal: Li Ju, because his numbers were too few to accomplish merit, often sighed in generous indignation.
translations.idiomatic: His force was too slight to win lasting fame, and he often broke into bitter, helpless sighs.

sentences.zh: 及帝踐阼，以為都督司州諸軍事、司州刺史，改封平陽縣侯，將軍如故。

translations.literal: When the emperor ascended the throne, he appointed Li Ju supervisor of military affairs for Si province, inspector of Si province, changed his fief to county marquis of Pingyang, and his generalship remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: At the new emperor's accession Li Ju became area commander for Si province and its inspector, traded his title for marquis of Pingyang county, and kept his old general's rank.

sentences.zh: 時弘農太守尹安、振威將軍宋始等四軍並屯洛陽，各相疑阻，莫有固志。

translations.literal: At that time prefect of Hongnong Yin An, General Who Rouses Might Song Shi, and four armies together were encamped at Luoyang; each suspected and blocked the others and none had a firm will to defend.
translations.idiomatic: Hongnong prefect Yin An, Song Shi the General Who Rouses Might, and two other columns all camped at Luoyang, eyeing one another with suspicion and no stomach for a stand.

sentences.zh: 矩、默各遣千騎至洛以鎮之。

translations.literal: Li Ju and Guo Mo each sent a thousand horsemen to Luoyang to stabilize them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju and Guo Mo each detached a thousand riders to steady the garrison.

sentences.zh: 安等乃同謀告石勒，勒遣石生率騎五千至洛陽，矩、默軍皆退還。

translations.literal: Yin An and the others then conspired together to inform Shi Le; Shi Le sent Shi Sheng with five thousand horsemen to Luoyang, and Li Ju's and Mo's armies both withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yin An and his fellows then jointly tipped off Shi Le, who sent Shi Sheng with five thousand horse; Li Ju and Guo Mo both pulled their men back.

sentences.zh: 俄而四將復背勒，遣使乞迎，默又遣步卒五百人入洛。

translations.literal: Soon the four generals again betrayed Shi Le, sent envoys begging to be taken in, and Mo again sent five hundred foot soldiers into Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the four commanders turned on Shi Le again, begged for rescue, and Guo Mo pushed another five hundred foot into the city.

sentences.zh: 石生以四將相謀，不能自安，乃虜宋始一軍，渡河而南。

translations.literal: Shi Sheng, because the four generals were plotting together, could not feel secure; he therefore captured Song Shi's entire army, crossed the river, and went south.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sheng, unnerved by their collusion, seized Song Shi's whole command, forded south, and quit the city.

sentences.zh: 百姓相率歸矩，於是洛中遂空。

translations.literal: The common people in companies attached themselves to Li Ju, and thereby Luoyang became empty.
translations.idiomatic: The townspeople streamed to Li Ju until Luoyang stood hollow.

sentences.zh: 矩乃表郭誦為揚武將軍、陽翟令，阻水築壘，且耕且守，為滅賊之計。

translations.literal: Li Ju thereupon memorialized recommending Guo Song as General Who Rouses Might and magistrate of Yangzhai, dammed the water and built ramparts, simultaneously farming and defending, as a plan to destroy the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He then recommended Guo Song for General Who Rouses Might and magistrate of Yangzhai, had him throw up dikes and forts along the water, plow and hold the line, and starve the enemy out.

sentences.zh: 屬趙固死，石生遣騎襲誦，誦多計略，賊至，輒設伏破之，虜掠無所得。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhao Gu died; Shi Sheng sent cavalry to raid Song; Song was full of stratagems—whenever the bandits came he laid ambushes and defeated them, and they obtained nothing from plundering.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Gu died, Shi Sheng sent raiders against Guo Song, who was never short of tricks—each attack walked into an ambush and came away empty-handed.

sentences.zh: 生怒，又自率四千餘騎暴掠諸縣，因攻誦壘，接戰須臾，退軍堮阪。

translations.literal: Sheng was angry and again personally led more than four thousand horsemen to ravage the counties, then attacked Song's fort; they joined battle briefly, then withdrew the army to the slope at Eban.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, Shi Sheng led over four thousand horse on a sweep of the countryside, then stormed Guo Song's walls; after a short clash he drew off to the Eban ridge.

sentences.zh: 誦率勁勇五百追及生於磐脂故亭，又大破之。

translations.literal: Song led five hundred picked braves, overtook Sheng at the old pavilion of Panzhi, and again greatly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Song took five hundred of his best fighters, ran Shi Sheng down at the old Panczhi post station, and thrashed him again.

sentences.zh: 矩以誦功多，表加赤幢曲蓋，封吉陽亭侯。

translations.literal: Li Ju, because Song's merit was great, memorialized adding crimson canopy and curved cover and enfeoffing him as village marquis of Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju cited Guo Song's heavy service and won him a crimson command canopy plus village marquis of Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 郭默欲侵祖約，矩禁之不可，遂為約所破。

translations.literal: Guo Mo wished to invade Zu Yue; Li Ju forbade him but could not stop him, and he was therefore defeated by Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Mo meant to strike Zu Yue; Li Ju forbade it but could not hold him, and Mo was shattered.

sentences.zh: 石勒遣其養子匆襲默，默懼後患未已，將降于劉曜，遣參軍鄭雄詣矩謀之，矩距而不許。

translations.literal: Shi Le sent his adopted son Cong to raid Mo; Mo feared later troubles would not end and was about to surrender to Liu Yao; he sent adjutant Zheng Xiong to Li Ju to plan it, but Li Ju refused and would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le dispatched his foster son Shi Cong against him; dreading an endless vendetta, Guo Mo prepared to go over to Liu Yao and sent Zheng Xiong to sound Li Ju out, but Li Ju turned him down flat.

sentences.zh: 後勒遣其將石良率精兵五千襲矩，矩逆擊不利。

translations.literal: Later Shi Le sent his general Shi Liang with five thousand picked troops to raid Li Ju; Li Ju met them in a counterattack but fared badly.
translations.idiomatic: Later Shi Le sent Shi Liang with five thousand veterans against Li Ju, who met them head-on and lost.

sentences.zh: 郭誦弟元復為賊所執，賊遣元以書說矩曰：「去年東平曹嶷，西賓猗盧，矩如牛角，何不歸命？

translations.literal: Guo Song's younger brother Yuan was again taken by the bandits; the bandits sent Yuan with a letter to persuade Li Ju, saying: "Last year to the east you had Cao Yi of Dongping, to the west you guested Yilu—Li Ju, you are like a horn between them—why not submit to the command?
translations.idiomatic: The enemy captured Guo Song's brother Yuan and sent him with a letter: "Eastward you feuded with Cao Yi of Dongping, westward you leaned on Yilu—you stand between them like a cow's horn—why not bend the knee?

sentences.zh: 」矩以示誦，誦曰：「昔王陵母在賊，猶不改意，弟當何論！

translations.literal: Li Ju showed it to Song; Song said: "In olden days Wang Ling's mother was in the enemy's hands and he still did not change his resolve—what is there to say of a younger brother!
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju showed Guo Song the letter. Song answered, "Wang Ling kept his loyalty even when his mother was hostage—why should a brother weigh more?

sentences.zh: 」勒復遺誦麈尾馬鞭，以示殷勤，誦不答。

translations.literal: Shi Le again sent Song a horsetail flywhisk and riding crop to show earnest goodwill; Song did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le followed with a flywhisk and whip as gifts of courtesy; Guo Song never answered.

sentences.zh: 勒將石生屯洛陽，大掠河南，矩、默大饑，默因復說矩降曜。

translations.literal: Shi Le's general Shi Sheng was encamped at Luoyang, greatly plundering Henan; Li Ju and Mo were in great famine, and Mo therefore again urged Li Ju to surrender to Yao.
translations.idiomatic: While Shi Sheng held Luoyang and stripped Henan bare, Li Ju and Guo Mo starved, and Mo again talked of defecting to Liu Yao.

sentences.zh: 矩既為石良所破,遂從默計，遣使於曜。

translations.literal: Li Ju, having already been defeated by Shi Liang, followed Mo's plan and sent envoys to Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Broken by Shi Liang, Li Ju yielded to Guo Mo and sent feelers to Liu Yao.

sentences.zh: 曜遣從弟岳軍于河陰，欲與矩謀攻石生。

translations.literal: Yao sent his cousin Yue with an army at Heyin, wishing to join Li Ju in planning an attack on Shi Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao posted his cousin Liu Yue on the north bank at Heyin to concert with Li Ju a strike on Shi Sheng.

sentences.zh: 勒遣將圍岳，嶽閉門不敢出。

translations.literal: Shi Le sent generals to besiege Yue; Yue closed the gates and dared not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le ringed Liu Yue with troops; Liu Yue shut his gates and refused to sortie.

sentences.zh: 默後為石匆所敗，自密南奔建康。

translations.literal: Mo was later defeated by Shi Cong and fled south from Mi to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Mo was later beaten by Shi Cong and ran south from Mi toward Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 矩聞之大怒，遣其將郭誦等齎書與默，又敕誦曰：「汝識脣亡之談不？

translations.literal: When Li Ju heard this he was greatly angry, sent his general Guo Song and others bearing a letter to Mo, and also instructed Song: "Do you understand the talk of lips and teeth perishing together?
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju, hearing of it, flew into a rage. He sent Guo Song with a letter for Guo Mo and warned him, "Have you forgotten how teeth and lips fall together?

sentences.zh: 迎接郭默，皆由於卿，臨難逃走，其必留之。

translations.literal: The welcoming of Guo Mo was entirely because of you; facing peril you fled away—you are sure to have left him in the lurch.
translations.idiomatic: You alone talked me into sheltering Guo Mo; when danger came you bolted and abandoned him.

sentences.zh: 」誦追及襄城，默自知負矩，棄妻子而遁。

translations.literal: Song overtook him at Xiangcheng; Mo, knowing he had wronged Li Ju, abandoned wife and children and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Song overtook him at Xiangcheng; knowing he had betrayed Li Ju, Guo Mo deserted his family and ran.

sentences.zh: 誦擁其餘眾而歸，矩待其妻子如初。

translations.literal: Song gathered his remaining host and returned; Li Ju treated his wife and children as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Song rounded up the stragglers and marched home; Li Ju sheltered Guo Mo's wife and children as before.

sentences.zh: 劉嶽以外援不至，降于石季龍。

translations.literal: Liu Yue, because outer aid did not arrive, surrendered to Shi Jilong.
translations.idiomatic: With no relief column coming, Liu Yue yielded to Shi Hu.

sentences.zh: 矩所統將士有陰欲歸勒者，矩知之而不能討，乃率眾南走，將歸朝廷，眾皆道亡，惟郭誦及參軍郭方，功曹張景，主簿苟遠，將軍騫韜、江霸、梁志、司馬尚、季弘、李瑰、段秀等百餘人棄家送矩。

translations.literal: Among the officers and soldiers Li Ju commanded, some secretly wished to join Shi Le; Li Ju knew it but could not punish them; he therefore led the host south, intending to return to the court; all along the road they deserted, and only Guo Song, adjutant Guo Fang, merit clerk Zhang Jing, secretary Gou Yuan, generals Qian Tao, Jiang Ba, Liang Zhi, Sima Shang, Ji Hong, Li Gui, Duan Xiu, and more than a hundred others abandoned their homes to escort Li Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Some of Li Ju's men were slipping away to Shi Le; he saw it but dared not purge them, so he struck south for the capital. The army melted away on the march until only Guo Song, Guo Fang, Zhang Jing, Gou Yuan, Qian Tao, Jiang Ba, Liang Zhi, Sima Shang, Ji Hong, Li Gui, Duan Xiu, and a hundred-odd loyalists forsook home to stay with him.

sentences.zh: 至於魯陽縣，矩墜馬卒，葬襄陽之峴山。

translations.literal: When they reached Luyang county, Li Ju fell from a horse and died; he was buried on Xian Mountain at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: At Luyang he was thrown from his horse and died; they laid him on Xian Hill outside Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 段匹磾

translations.literal: Duan Pidi
translations.idiomatic: Duan Pidi

sentences.zh: 段匹磾，東部鮮卑人也。

translations.literal: Duan Pidi was a man of the eastern-branch Xianbei.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Pidi belonged to the eastern branch of the Xianbei.

sentences.zh: 種類勁健，世為大人。

translations.literal: His kind was stalwart; for generations they had been great chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: His people were fierce horsemen who for generations had ruled as chieftains.

sentences.zh: 父務勿塵，遣軍助東海王越征討有功，王浚表為親晉王，封遼西公，嫁女與務勿塵，以結鄰援。

translations.literal: His father Wuwuchen sent troops to aid Prince Donghai Sima Yue in campaigns and had merit; Wang Jun memorialized him as king friendly to the Jin, enfeoffed him duke of Liaoxi, married a daughter to Wuwuchen, and thereby cemented a neighboring alliance.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wuwuchen had sent warriors to fight beside Prince Donghai Sima Yue; Wang Jun had him titled the Jin-allied king, created duke of Liaoxi, and married him a daughter to seal the frontier pact.

sentences.zh: 懷帝即位，以務勿塵為大單于，匹磾為左賢王，率眾助國征討，假撫軍大將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huai ascended the throne, he appointed Wuwuchen grand shanyu and Pidi left worthy king, led the host to aid the state in campaigns, and provisionally named him grand general who comforts the army.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huai named Wuwuchen grand chanyu and Pidi left worthy king, brought their tribes in on imperial campaigns, and gave Pidi the acting title grand general who comforts the army.

sentences.zh: 務勿塵死，弟涉復辰以務勿塵子疾陸眷襲號。

translations.literal: When Wuwuchen died, his younger brother Shefuchen had Wuwuchen's son Jilujuan inherit the title.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuwuchen died, his brother Shefuchen installed Wuwuchen's son Jilujuan as heir.

sentences.zh: 劉曜逼洛陽，王浚遣督護王昌等率疾陸眷及弟文鴦、從弟末杯攻石勒于襄國。

translations.literal: When Liu Yao pressed Luoyang, Wang Jun sent supervisor Wang Chang and others to lead Jilujuan and his younger brother Wenying and cousin Mobo to attack Shi Le at Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: As Liu Yao closed on Luoyang, Wang Jun dispatched Wang Chang to lead Jilujuan, Wenying, and Mobo against Shi Le at Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 勒敗還壘，末杯追入壘門，為勒所獲。

translations.literal: Le was defeated and returned to his fort; Mobo pursued into the fort gate and was captured by Le.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le fell back to his ramparts; Mobo chased through the gate and was taken alive.

sentences.zh: 勒質末杯，遣使求和于疾陸眷，疾陸眷將許之，文鴦諫曰：「受命討勒，寧以末杯一人，故縱成擒之冠？

translations.literal: Le held Mobo hostage and sent an envoy to sue for peace with Jilujuan; Jilujuan was about to consent when Wenying remonstrated: "We received orders to punish Shi Le—would you for Mobo alone release a foe already in the bag?
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le held Mobo hostage and sued for peace; Jilujuan was ready to agree when Wenying objected: "We were ordered to crush Shi Le—would you loose a cornered prey for one man?

sentences.zh: 既失浚意，且有後憂，必不可許。

translations.literal: You will both lose Wang Jun's favor and afterward have later worries—it absolutely cannot be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: You would forfeit Wang Jun's trust and court future peril—this must not be allowed.

sentences.zh: 」疾陸眷不聽，以鎧馬二百五十匹、金銀各一簏贈末杯。

translations.literal: Jilujuan did not listen; he presented two hundred fifty armored horses and one basket each of gold and silver to ransom Mobo.
translations.idiomatic: Jilujuan refused the counsel and sent two hundred fifty barded horses plus baskets of gold and silver to buy Mobo back.

sentences.zh: 勒歸之，又厚以金寶采絹報疾陸眷。

translations.literal: Le returned him and in turn richly repaid Jilujuan with gold, jewels, and colored silk.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le released him and heaped gold, gems, and brocades on Jilujuan in return.

sentences.zh: 疾陸眷令文鴦與石季龍同盟，約為兄弟，遂引騎還。

translations.literal: Jilujuan ordered Wenying to ally with Shi Jilong by oath as brothers, then led the horsemen back.
translations.idiomatic: Jilujuan had Wenying swear brotherhood with Shi Hu and then marched his cavalry home.

sentences.zh: 昌等不能獨守，亦還。

translations.literal: Chang and the others could not hold alone and likewise returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chang could not hold the field alone and withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 建武初，匹磾推劉琨為大都督，結盟討勒，並檄涉復辰、疾陸眷、末杯等三面俱集襄國，琨、匹磾進屯固安，以候眾軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu, Pidi promoted Liu Kun as grand commander-in-chief, formed an alliance to punish Shi Le, and jointly summoned Shefuchen, Jilujuan, Mobo, and others so that three sides would all gather at Xiangguo; Kun and Pidi advanced and encamped at Gu'an to await the assembled armies.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianwu era Pidi raised Liu Kun to supreme commander, forged a league against Shi Le, and called Shefuchen, Jilujuan, and Mobo to converge on Xiangguo from three directions while he and Liu Kun camped at Gu'an to wait for them.

sentences.zh: 勒懼，遣間使厚賂末杯。

translations.literal: Le feared and sent a secret envoy with rich bribes to Mobo.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le, alarmed, slipped Mobo a heavy bribe through a covert messenger.

sentences.zh: 然末杯既思報其舊恩，且因匹磾在外，欲襲奪其國，乃間匹磾於涉復辰、疾陸眷曰：「以父兄而從子弟邪？

translations.literal: Yet Mobo both wished to repay an old kindness and, moreover, because Pidi was abroad, wished to surprise-seize his state; he therefore slandered Pidi to Shefuchen and Jilujuan, saying: "To follow sons and younger brothers on account of fathers and elder brothers?
translations.idiomatic: Mobo meant both to repay an old debt and, with Pidi away, to seize his domain; he whispered to Shefuchen and Jilujuan, "Why should fathers and uncles take orders from sons and nephews?

sentences.zh: 雖一旦有功，匹磾獨收之矣。

translations.literal: Even if in one morning there is merit, Pidi alone will harvest it.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the day brings victory, Pidi alone will pocket the glory.

sentences.zh: 」涉復辰等以為然，引軍而還。

translations.literal: Shefuchen and the others held it right and led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Shefuchen and his kin thought him right and marched home.

sentences.zh: 匹磾亦止。

translations.literal: Pidi likewise halted.
translations.idiomatic: Pidi too stopped in his tracks.

sentences.zh: 會疾陸眷病死，匹磾自薊奔喪，至於右北平。

translations.literal: It happened that Jilujuan died of illness; Pidi from Ji hurried to the mourning and reached Youbeiping.
translations.idiomatic: When Jilujuan died, Pidi raced from Ji to the funeral and reached Youbeiping.

sentences.zh: 末杯宣言匹磾將篡，出軍擊敗之。

translations.literal: Mobo publicly declared Pidi was about to usurp, marched out, and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Mobo accused Pidi of plotting usurpation, took the field, and broke his force.

sentences.zh: 末杯遂害涉復辰及其子弟黨與二百餘人，自立為單于。

translations.literal: Mobo thereupon killed Shefuchen and more than two hundred of his sons, younger kin, and faction, and established himself as shanyu.
translations.idiomatic: He then slaughtered Shefuchen, over two hundred sons and followers, and declared himself chanyu.

sentences.zh: 及王浚敗，匹磾領幽州刺史，劉琨自并州依之，復與匹磾結盟，俱討石勒。

translations.literal: When Wang Jun was defeated, Pidi took the office of inspector of You province; Liu Kun from Bing province relied on him and again allied with Pidi, both together campaigning against Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Jun's fall Pidi became inspector of You; Liu Kun came down from Bing to lean on him, and the two renewed their pact against Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 匹磾復為末杯所敗，士眾離散，懼琨圖己，遂害之，於是晉人離散矣。

translations.literal: Pidi was again defeated by Mobo; his soldiers and host scattered; fearing Kun would plot against him, he thereupon killed him, and thereby Jin people scattered apart.
translations.idiomatic: Pidi lost again to Mobo and his army melted away; dreading Liu Kun's designs, he murdered him, and the Chinese followers drifted away.

sentences.zh: 匹磾不能自固，北依邵續，末杯又攻敗之。

translations.literal: Pidi could not secure himself and fled north to rely on Shao Xu; Mobo again attacked and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to stand alone, Pidi fled north to Shao Xu; Mobo struck him once more and broke him.

sentences.zh: 匹磾被瘡，謂續曰：「吾夷狄慕義，以至破家，君若不忘舊要，與吾進討，君之惠也。

translations.literal: Pidi, wounded, said to Xu: "We barbarians admired righteousness until our families were broken; if you do not forget the old compact and join me in advancing the punishment, it will be your grace.
translations.idiomatic: Wounded, Pidi told Shao Xu, "We steppe folk clung to honor until our houses were ruined; if you still honor our old pledge and march with me against the foe, you will do me the greatest kindness.

sentences.zh: 」續曰：「賴公威德，續得效節。

translations.literal: Xu said: "Relying on your awesome virtue, Xu was able to devote his utmost loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Xu replied, "It was your prestige that let me serve the throne at all.

sentences.zh: 今公有難，豈敢不俱！

translations.literal: Now the lord is in difficulty—how could I dare not go together!
translations.idiomatic: Now you are in peril—how could I hang back?

sentences.zh: 」遂並力追末杯，斬獲略盡。

translations.literal: Thereupon they joined strength pursuing Mobo, killing and capturing nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: They joined forces, ran Mobo down, and killed or captured almost every man.

sentences.zh: 又令文鴦北討末杯弟于薊城，及還，去城八十里，聞續已沒，眾懼而散，復為石季龍所遮，文鴦以其親兵數百人力戰破之，始得入城。

translations.literal: He also ordered Wenying north to punish Mobo's younger brother at Ji city; when returning, eighty li from the city, hearing Xu had already been lost, the host feared and scattered, and again was intercepted by Shi Jilong; Wenying with several hundred of his personal guard fought bitterly, broke them, and only then was able to enter the city.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wenying north against Mobo's brother at Ji; on the way back, eighty li from the walls, word came that Shao Xu had fallen—the army panicked and broke. Shi Hu barred the road, but Wenying cut through with a few hundred household guards and fought his way inside.

sentences.zh: 季龍復抄城下，文鴦登城臨見，欲出擊之，匹磾不許。

translations.literal: Shi Jilong again raided beneath the walls; Wenying ascended the walls and looked down, wishing to go out and strike them, but Pidi did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu raided the suburbs again; Wenying mounted the wall, itching to sortie, but Pidi forbade it.

sentences.zh: 文鴦曰：「我以勇聞，故百姓杖我。

translations.literal: Wenying said: "I am famed for courage; therefore the common people lean on me.
translations.idiomatic: Wenying said, "My name is courage—the people lean on me for that.

sentences.zh: 見人被略而不救，非丈夫也。

translations.literal: To see people carried off and not rescue them is not the conduct of a man.
translations.idiomatic: To watch folk dragged away and do nothing is unworthy of a man.

sentences.zh: 令眾失望，誰復為我致死乎！

translations.literal: If the host loses hope, who again will die for me!
translations.idiomatic: If the army loses heart, who will die for me again?

sentences.zh: 」遂將壯士數十騎出戰，殺胡甚多。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led several tens of stalwart horsemen out to battle and killed very many Hu.
translations.idiomatic: He led several dozen picked horsemen out and piled Hu corpses high.

sentences.zh: 遇馬乏，伏不能起。

translations.literal: His horse grew exhausted and fell; he could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: His mount gave out and threw him; he could not remount.

sentences.zh: 季龍呼曰：「大兄與我俱是戎狄，久望共同。

translations.literal: Shi Jilong called out: "Elder brother and I are both Rong and Di; for long I have hoped we might share the same path.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu shouted, "We are both steppe men; I have long wanted us on the same side.

sentences.zh: 天不違願，今日相見，何故復戰？

translations.literal: Heaven has not opposed the wish—today we meet face to face; for what reason do we fight again?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven grants the meeting—why trade blows now?

sentences.zh: 請釋杖。

translations.literal: Please lay down the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Drop your lance.

sentences.zh: 」文鴦罵曰：「汝為寇虐，久應合死，吾兄不用吾計，故令汝得至此，吾寧死，不為汝擒。

translations.literal: Wenying cursed him: "You have acted the bandit tyrant and long ago deserved death; my elder brother did not use my plan, therefore he let you reach this point; I would rather die than be captured by you.
translations.idiomatic: Wenying snarled back, "You have ravaged like a wolf and earned death a hundred times; my brother spurned my counsel and let you come this far—I will die before I let you take me.

sentences.zh: 」遂下馬苦戰，槊折，執刀力戰不已。

translations.literal: Thereupon he dismounted and fought bitterly on foot; his lance broke; grasping a knife he fought on without stopping.
translations.idiomatic: He leapt down to fight on foot; his spear snapped, so he seized a knife and kept slashing.

sentences.zh: 季龍軍四面解馬羅披自鄣，前捉文鴦。

translations.literal: Shi Jilong's army on four sides loosened horse nets and leather screens to shield themselves and advanced to seize Wenying.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu's men ringed him with horse ropes and leather screens, then closed to seize him.

sentences.zh: 文鴦戰自辰至申，力極而後被執。

translations.literal: Wenying fought from the chen hour to the shen hour; only when his strength was exhausted was he at last captured.
translations.idiomatic: He fought from dawn past noon until strength failed and they took him.

sentences.zh: 城內大懼。

translations.literal: Inside the city there was great fear.
translations.idiomatic: Panic swept the walls.

sentences.zh: 匹磾欲單騎歸朝，續弟樂安內史洎協兵，不許，洎復欲執臺使王英送于季龍，匹磾正色責之曰：「卿不能遵兄之志，逼吾不得歸朝，亦以甚矣，復欲執天子使者，我雖胡素，所未聞也。

translations.literal: Pidi wished to ride alone to the court; Shao Xu's younger brother, interior governor of Le'an, Ji, coordinated troops and would not permit it; Ji again wished to seize court envoy Wang Ying and deliver him to Shi Jilong; Pidi with stern countenance rebuked him, saying: "You cannot follow your elder brother's will, forcing me so I cannot return to the court—that is already extreme; again you wish to seize the Son of Heaven's envoy—although I am a Hu by birth, I have never heard of such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Pidi meant to ride alone to the Jin court, but Shao Xu's brother Ji, interior governor of Le'an, mobilized troops and barred the way; Ji even meant to seize imperial envoy Wang Ying and hand him to Shi Hu. Pidi rebuked him coldly: "You refuse your brother's purpose and block me from the capital—that is bad enough; now you would lay hands on the emperor's messenger. I am a barbarian by blood, yet even I have never heard the like.

sentences.zh: 」因謂英曰：「匹磾世受重恩，不忘忠孝。

translations.literal: Thereupon he said to Ying: "Pidi's family for generations has received heavy favor and does not forget loyalty and filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Turning to Wang Ying he said, "My house has eaten the Jin's bounty for generations; we have not forgotten loyalty or duty.

sentences.zh: 今日事逼，欲歸罪朝廷，而見逼迫，忠款不遂。

translations.literal: Today affairs press me; I wished to return blame to the court, yet I am pressed and blocked; my loyal sincerity cannot be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Circumstances drive me now—I would lay my guilt before the throne, yet I am hemmed in until my good faith cannot reach it.

sentences.zh: 若得假息，未死之日，心不忘本。

translations.literal: If I can obtain borrowed rest, on days before death my heart will not forget its root.
translations.idiomatic: If I gain a little breathing space, I shall not forget where I came from while I still draw breath.

sentences.zh: 」遂渡黃河南。

translations.literal: Thereupon he crossed the Yellow River southward.
translations.idiomatic: He then forded the Yellow River to the south.

sentences.zh: 匹磾著朝服，持節，賓從出見季龍曰：「我受國恩，志在滅汝。

translations.literal: Pidi put on court robes, grasped the credential, and with guests and followers went out to see Shi Jilong, saying: "I received the state's grace; my will was to destroy you.
translations.idiomatic: In full court dress, baton in hand, he stepped out with his train to face Shi Hu and said, "The dynasty favored me; I meant to destroy you.

sentences.zh: 不幸吾國自亂，以至於此。

translations.literal: Unluckily my state fell into internal disorder, so that it reached this point.
translations.idiomatic: My own people tore themselves apart until we came to this pass.

sentences.zh: 既不能死，又不能為汝敬也。

translations.literal: I can neither die nor bow in respect to you.
translations.idiomatic: I can neither die a clean death nor bow to you.

sentences.zh: 」勒及季龍素與匹磾結為兄弟，季龍起而拜之。

translations.literal: Shi Le and Shi Jilong had of old sworn brotherhood with Pidi; Shi Jilong rose and bowed to him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le and Shi Hu had once sworn brotherhood with him; Shi Hu rose and bowed.

sentences.zh: 匹磾到襄國，又不為勒禮，常著朝服，持晉節。

translations.literal: When Pidi arrived at Xiangguo, again he did not perform courtesy to Shi Le; he constantly wore court robes and held the Jin credential.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiangguo he still refused to humble himself before Shi Le, going about in Jin court dress with the Jin baton in hand.

sentences.zh: 經年，國中謀推匹磾為主，事露，被害。

translations.literal: After a full year, in the state a plot to promote Pidi as lord leaked out, and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: A year later a plot to make him ruler came to light and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 文鴦亦遇鴆而死，惟末波存焉。

translations.literal: Wenying likewise met death by poisoned wine; only Mobo survived.
translations.idiomatic: Wenying too was poisoned; only Mobo was left alive.

sentences.zh: 及死，弟牙立。

translations.literal: When he died, his younger brother Ya succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Mobo died, his brother Ya inherited.

sentences.zh: 牙死，其後從祖就陸眷之孫遼立。

translations.literal: When Ya died, afterward Liao, grandson of Jiulujuan on the collateral line, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Ya's death left the chieftaincy to Liao, a grandson of the Jiulujuan branch.

sentences.zh: 自務勿塵已後，值晉喪亂，自稱位號，據有遼西之地，而臣禦晉人。

translations.literal: From Wuwuchen onward, encountering the Jin's ruin and chaos, they styled themselves with titles and ranks, occupied the land west of Liaoxi, and ruled over Jin people as subjects.
translations.idiomatic: From Wuwuchen's day through the Jin collapse they styled themselves kings, held western Liaoxi, and governed their Chinese subjects in feudal order.

sentences.zh: 其地西盡幽州，東界遼水。

translations.literal: Their territory reached west to the limit of You province and east bordered the Liao River.
translations.idiomatic: Their realm ran west to the edge of You and east to the Liao River.

sentences.zh: 然所統胡晉可三萬餘家，控弦可四五萬騎，而與石季龍遞相侵掠，連兵不息，竟為季龍所破，徙其遺黎數萬家于司雍之地。

translations.literal: Yet those they ruled, Hu and Jin together, were more than thirty thousand households; bowstrings drawn could be forty or fifty thousand horsemen; yet with Shi Jilong they repeatedly raided each other in turn; arms did not cease; in the end they were broken by Shi Jilong, who moved their surviving common people, several tens of thousands of households, to the lands of Si and Yong.
translations.idiomatic: They counted some thirty thousand Hu and Chinese households and forty or fifty thousand archers on horseback, yet they skirmished endlessly with Shi Hu until he broke them and deported tens of thousands of survivors into Si and Yong.

sentences.zh: 其子蘭復聚兵，與季龍為患久之。

translations.literal: His son Lan again gathered troops and for a long time was a trouble to Shi Jilong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lan rallied another army and plagued Shi Hu for years.

sentences.zh: 及石氏之亡，末波之子勤鳩集胡羯得萬餘人，保枉人山，自稱趙王，附于慕容俊。

translations.literal: When the Shi clan perished, Mobo's son Qin gathered Hu and Jie to more than ten thousand men, held Mount Wangren, styled himself king of Zhao, and attached himself to Murong Jun.
translations.idiomatic: After the Shi fell, Mobo's son Qin mustered over ten thousand Hu and Jie on Mount Wangren, declared himself king of Zhao, and submitted to Murong Jun.

sentences.zh: 俄為冉閔所敗，徙於繹幕，僭即尊號。

translations.literal: Soon he was defeated by Ran Min and moved to Yimu, usurping the supreme title.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min soon broke him and drove him to Yimu, where he claimed the imperial style.

sentences.zh: 俊遣慕容恪擊之，勤懼而降。

translations.literal: Jun sent Murong Ke to strike him; Qin feared and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun sent Murong Ke against him; Qin yielded in terror.

sentences.zh: 魏浚

translations.literal: Wei Jun
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jun

sentences.zh: 魏浚，東郡東阿人也，寓居關中。

translations.literal: Wei Jun was a man of Dong'e in Dong commandery and sojourned in Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jun came from Dong'e in the eastern commandery but had settled in Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 初為雍州小吏，河間王顒敗亂之際，以為武威將軍。

translations.literal: At first he was a petty clerk in Yong province; during the defeat and turmoil of Prince Hejian Sima Yong, he was appointed General Who Displays Might.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a minor clerk in Yong; amid Prince Hejian Sima Yong's defeat he was named General Who Displays Might.

sentences.zh: 後為度支校尉，有幹用。

translations.literal: Later he became commissary colonel and had administrative ability.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to commissary colonel and proved capable in office.

sentences.zh: 永嘉末，與流人數百家東保河陰之硤石。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongjia, with several hundred households of displaced persons he went east to protect Xiashi on the Yin of the Yellow River's north bank.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Yongjia era he led several hundred refugee families east to hold the Xiashi defile north of the river.

sentences.zh: 時京邑荒儉，浚劫掠得穀麥，獻之懷帝，帝以為揚威將軍、平陽太守，度支如故。

translations.literal: At that time the capital district was desolate and straitened; Jun by plunder obtained grain and wheat, presented them to Emperor Huai, and the emperor appointed him General Who Rouses Might and prefect of Pingyang, his commissary post remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was starving; Wei Jun seized grain and sent it to Emperor Huai, who named him General Who Rouses Might and prefect of Pingyang while keeping him on supply duty.

sentences.zh: 以亂不之官。

translations.literal: Because of the turmoil he did not take up the office.
translations.idiomatic: The chaos kept him from taking his post.

sentences.zh: 及洛陽陷，屯於洛北石梁塢，撫養遺眾，漸修軍器。

translations.literal: When Luoyang fell, he encamped north of the Luo at the Stone Beam fort, comforted the surviving host, and gradually repaired military equipment.
translations.idiomatic: After Luoyang fell he built a fort on the stone bridge north of the river, gathered survivors, and slowly rebuilt an arsenal.

sentences.zh: 其附賊者，皆先解喻，說大晉運數靈長，行已建立，歸之者甚眾。

translations.literal: Those who had attached to the bandits he first explained and persuaded, declaring the great Jin's fortune long and numinous and that the ruler had already been established; those who returned were very many.
translations.idiomatic: To those who had served the rebels he preached that the great Jin still enjoyed Heaven's favor and a new emperor already sat on the throne; multitudes came back.

sentences.zh: 其有恃遠不從命者，遣將討之，服從而已，不加侵暴。

translations.literal: Those who relied on distance and did not obey orders he sent generals to punish; once they submitted he stopped and did not add invasion or violence.
translations.idiomatic: Defiant holdouts he chastised by arms, then stopped the moment they yielded, without needless cruelty.

sentences.zh: 於是遠近感悅，繈負至者漸眾。

translations.literal: Thereby near and far were moved and pleased, and those who arrived carrying infants on their backs gradually grew numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Word spread, and refugees with children on their backs streamed to him.

sentences.zh: 劉琨承制，假浚河南尹。

translations.literal: Liu Kun, exercising plenipotentiary command, provisionally appointed Jun metropolitan governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun in plenipotentiary orders made him acting metropolitan governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 時太尉荀籓建行臺在密縣，浚詣籓諮謀軍事，籓甚悅，要李矩同會。

translations.literal: At that time grand commandant Xun Fan had set up a mobile headquarters at Mi county; Jun went to Fan to consult on military affairs; Fan was greatly pleased and invited Li Ju to meet together.
translations.idiomatic: Grand commandant Xun Fan had a field headquarters at Mi; Wei Jun rode there to plan strategy. Fan was delighted and asked Li Ju to join the council.

sentences.zh: 矩將夜赴之，矩官屬以浚不可信，不宜夜往。

translations.literal: Ju was about to go by night; Ju's subordinates held that Jun could not be trusted and it was not fitting to go by night.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju meant to travel by night, but his staff said Wei Jun was untrustworthy and a night ride unwise.

sentences.zh: 矩曰：「忠臣同心，將何疑乎！

translations.literal: Ju said: "Loyal ministers share one heart—what is there to doubt!
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju answered, "Loyal men share one mind—what is there to fear!"

sentences.zh: 」及會，客主盡歎，浚因與矩相結而去。

translations.literal: When they met, guest and host all sighed in admiration; Jun therefore formed ties with Ju and departed.
translations.idiomatic: At the meeting host and guests were moved alike; Wei Jun and Li Ju swore friendship and parted.

sentences.zh: 劉曜忌浚得眾，率眾軍圍之。

translations.literal: Liu Yao resented Jun's winning the host and led an army to besiege him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao, jealous of his following, brought an army to besiege him.

sentences.zh: 劉演、郭默遣軍來救，曜分兵逆于河北，乃伏兵深隱處，以邀演、默軍，大破之，盡虜演等騎。
