translations.literal: Liu Yan and Guo Mo sent troops to relieve him; Yao divided troops to intercept north of the River, then ambushed in a deeply hidden place to intercept Yan's and Mo's army, greatly defeated them, and fully captured Yan and the others' cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan and Guo Mo sent relief, but Liu Yao split a force to block the north bank, laid an ambush in rough country, shattered the column, and took every horseman of Yan's command.

sentences.zh: 浚夜遁走，為曜所得，遂死之。

translations.literal: Jun fled by night, was taken by Yao, and thereupon died at his hands.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jun slipped away at night, fell into Liu Yao's hands, and died there.

sentences.zh: 追贈平西將軍。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously named him General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 族子該領其眾。

translations.literal: His agnate nephew Gai led his host.
translations.idiomatic: His kinsman Wei Gai took command of the remnant.

translations.literal: The received text marks a section division at this point.
translations.idiomatic: Here the manuscript sets off the following subsection.

sentences.zh: 族子該

translations.literal: Agnate nephew Gai
translations.idiomatic: Kinsman Wei Gai

sentences.zh: =該一名亥，本僑居京兆陰磐。

translations.literal: = Gai's other name was Hai; originally he sojourned at Yinpan in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gai was also called Hai and had lived as a sojourner at Yinpan in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 河間王顒之伐趙王倫，以該為將兵都尉。

translations.literal: When Prince Hejian Sima Yong campaigned against Prince Zhao Sima Lun, he appointed Gai colonel commanding troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Hejian marched against Prince Zhao, Sima Lun, he named Wei Gai colonel of troops.

sentences.zh: 及劉曜攻洛陽，隨浚赴難，先領兵守金墉城，故得無他。

translations.literal: When Liu Yao attacked Luoyang, he followed Jun to answer the crisis, first leading troops to defend the Metal Moat fort, therefore there was nothing else amiss.
translations.idiomatic: During Liu Yao's siege of Luoyang he rode with Wei Jun to the rescue and held the Metal Moat first, so the line held.

sentences.zh: 曜引去，餘眾依之。

translations.literal: Yao led his forces away; the remaining host relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yao drew off, the survivors rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 時杜預子尹為弘農太守，屯宜陽界一泉塢，數為諸賊所抄掠。

translations.literal: At that time Du Yin, son of Du Yu, was prefect of Hongnong, encamped at the Yiquan fort on the Yiyang border, and several times was raided by various bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu's son Yin held Hongnong from the Yiquan fort on the Yiyang border and suffered repeated bandit raids.

sentences.zh: 尹要該共距之，該遣其將馬瞻將三百人赴尹。

translations.literal: Yin invited Gai jointly to resist them; Gai sent his general Ma Zhan with three hundred men to go to Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yin called on Wei Gai for help; Gai sent Ma Zhan with three hundred men.

sentences.zh: 瞻知其無備，夜襲尹殺之，迎該據塢。

translations.literal: Zhan knew he was unprepared, raided Yin by night, killed him, and welcomed Gai to occupy the fort.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhan saw the garrison was slack, stormed it by night, murdered Du Yin, and installed Wei Gai in the fort.

sentences.zh: 塢人震懼，並服從之。

translations.literal: The people of the fort were shaken with fear and all submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders were terrified into submission.

sentences.zh: 乃與李炬、郭默相結以距賊。

translations.literal: Thereupon he formed ties with Li Ju and Guo Mo jointly to resist the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He then allied with Li Ju and Guo Mo against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 荀籓即以該為武威將軍，統城西雍涼人，使討劉曜。

translations.literal: Xun Fan immediately appointed Gai General Who Displays Might, commanding the Yong and Liang people west of the city, and had him campaign against Liu Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Fan at once named him General Who Displays Might over the western Yong and Liang communities and sent him against Liu Yao.

sentences.zh: 元帝承制，加冠軍將軍、河東太守。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan, exercising plenipotentiary command, added General Who Crowns the Army and prefect of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan in acting authority added General Who Crowns the Army and prefect of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 督護河東、河南、平陽三郡。

translations.literal: Chief of staff for Hedong, Henan, and Pingyang three commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He was given staff authority over Hedong, Henan, and Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 曜嘗攻李矩，該破之。

translations.literal: Yao once attacked Li Ju; Gai defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yao struck Li Ju, Wei Gai broke his attack.

sentences.zh: 及矩將迎郭默，該遣軍助之，又與河南尹任愔相連結。

translations.literal: When Ju was about to welcome Guo Mo, Gai sent troops to aid him, and again he linked with metropolitan governor of Henan Ren Yin.
translations.idiomatic: He sent troops to help Li Ju escort Guo Mo and joined Henan governor Ren Yin.

sentences.zh: 後漸饑弊，曜寇日至，欲率眾南徙，眾不從，該遂單騎走至南陽。

translations.literal: Later they gradually grew hungry and exhausted; Yao's raids came daily; he wished to lead the host south to migrate; the host would not follow; Gai thereupon alone on horseback fled to Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Starvation and Liu Yao's daily raids wore them down; when Wei Gai tried to move the army south, the men refused, and he fled alone to Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 帝又以為前鋒都督、平北將軍、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor again appointed him vanguard area commander, General Who Pacifies the North, and inspector of Yong province.
translations.idiomatic: The court named him vanguard commander, General Who Pacifies the North, and inspector of Yong.

sentences.zh: 馬瞻率該餘眾降曜。

translations.literal: Ma Zhan led Gai's remaining host and surrendered to Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhan led what was left of his force to Liu Yao.

sentences.zh: 曜徵發既苦，瞻又驕虐，部曲遣使呼該，該密往赴之，其眾殺瞻而納該。

translations.literal: Yao's levies were already bitter; Zhan again was arrogant and cruel; retainers sent envoys to summon Gai; Gai secretly went to join them; his host killed Zhan and welcomed Gai.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao's conscriptions had crushed the men, and Ma Zhan ruled them with cruelty until his officers secretly called Wei Gai back; they killed Ma Zhan and restored Gai.

sentences.zh: 該遷於新野，率眾助周訪討平杜曾，詔以該為順陽太守。

translations.literal: Gai moved to Xinye, led the host to aid Zhou Fang in punishing and pacifying Du Zeng, and an edict appointed Gai prefect of Shunyang.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew to Xinye, marched with Zhou Fang to crush Du Zeng, and was enfeoffed prefect of Shunyang.

sentences.zh: 王敦之反也，梁州刺史甘卓不從，欲觀該去就，試以敦旨動之。

translations.literal: When Wang Dun rebelled, inspector of Liang province Gan Zhuo did not follow; wishing to observe Gai's course, he tested him by moving him with Dun's order.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun rose, Gan Zhuo of Liang province stayed neutral and sounded Wei Gai with a forged order from Dun.

sentences.zh: 該曰：「我本去賊，惟忠於國。

translations.literal: Gai said: "I originally left the bandits—only loyalty to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gai replied, "I left the rebels to serve the throne alone.

sentences.zh: 今王公舉兵向天子，非吾所宜與也。

translations.literal: Now the prince duke raises troops against the Son of Heaven—it is not what I ought to join.
translations.idiomatic: Now a prince marches on the emperor—nothing could make me take his part.

sentences.zh: 」遂距而不應。

translations.literal: Thereupon he refused and did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: He refused outright.

sentences.zh: 及蘇峻反，率眾救臺，軍次石頭，受陶侃節度。

translations.literal: When Su Jun rebelled, he led the host to rescue the terrace palaces; the army halted at Stone Fort and received Tao Kan's command.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Jun mutinied he brought his men to relieve the palace, halted at Stone City, and served under Tao Kan.

sentences.zh: 峻未平，該病篤還屯，卒於道，葬于武陵。

translations.literal: Before Jun was pacified, Gai, gravely ill, returned to encampment, died on the road, and was buried at Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun was still in the field when Wei Gai, mortally ill, turned for his camp, died on the march, and was buried at Wuling.

sentences.zh: 從子雄統其眾。

translations.literal: His agnate nephew Xiong commanded his host.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Wei Xiong inherited the command.

sentences.zh: 郭默

translations.literal: Guo Mo
translations.idiomatic: Guo Mo

sentences.zh: 郭默，河內懷人。

translations.literal: Guo Mo was a man of Huai in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Mo came from Huai in Henan.

sentences.zh: 少微賤，以壯勇事太守裴整，為督將。

translations.literal: In youth he was lowly and mean; with stalwart courage he served prefect Pei Zheng as chief of staff.
translations.idiomatic: Born poor, he won a place through sheer nerve as a staff commander under Prefect Pei Zheng.

sentences.zh: 永嘉之亂，默率遺眾自為塢主，以漁舟抄東歸行旅，積年遂致巨富，流人依附者漸眾。

translations.literal: In the Yongjia turmoil, Mo led the surviving host and made himself fort chief; using fishing boats he plundered eastbound travelers on the river; over years he thereby became enormously wealthy, and displaced persons who attached themselves gradually grew numerous.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongjia tore the realm apart he made himself lord of a river fort, robbed eastbound travelers from boats, grew rich over the years, and drew a swelling crowd of refugees.

sentences.zh: 撫循將士，甚得其歡心。

translations.literal: He comforted and guided officers and men and very much won their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: He knew how to handle his soldiers and kept their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 默婦兄同郡陸嘉取官米數石餉妹，默以為違制，將殺嘉，嘉懼，奔石勒。

translations.literal: Mo's wife's elder brother from the same commandery, Lu Jia, took several shi of official rice to feed his younger sister; Mo held it violated regulations and was about to kill Jia; Jia feared and fled to Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: His brother-in-law Lu Jia stole a few sacks of government grain for Mo's wife; Mo called it a capital offense. Lu Jia ran to Shi Le for his life.

sentences.zh: 默乃自射殺婦，以明無私。

translations.literal: Mo thereupon personally shot and killed his wife to show he had no private partiality.
translations.idiomatic: To prove his impartiality he shot his own wife dead.

sentences.zh: 遣使謁劉琨，琨加默河內太守。

translations.literal: He sent an envoy to visit Liu Kun; Kun added Mo as prefect of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to Liu Kun, who named him prefect of Henan.

sentences.zh: 劉元海遣從子曜討默，曜列三屯圍之，欲使餓死。

translations.literal: Liu Yuanhai sent his nephew Yao to punish Mo; Yao set three camps to besiege him, wishing to starve him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan sent Liu Yao against him; Yao ringed him with three camps and tried to starve him out.

sentences.zh: 默送妻子為質，並請糴焉，糴畢，設守。

translations.literal: Mo sent wife and children as hostages and also requested to buy grain; when the purchase was finished, he set defenses.
translations.idiomatic: He handed over his family as hostages, bought grain, then threw up defenses the moment the grain was in.

sentences.zh: 曜怒，沈默妻子于河而攻之。

translations.literal: Yao was angry, drowned Mo's wife and children in the river, and attacked him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao, furious, drowned his hostages and stormed the fort.

sentences.zh: 默遣弟芝求救于劉琨，琨知默狡猾，留之而緩其救。

translations.literal: Mo sent his younger brother Zhi to beg rescue from Liu Kun; Kun, knowing Mo was treacherous, detained him and delayed the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Mo sent his brother Zhi to Liu Kun for help; Kun, knowing Mo's cunning, held Zhi back and slow-walked the relief.

sentences.zh: 默更遣人告急。

translations.literal: Mo again sent men with urgent plea.
translations.idiomatic: Mo sent fresh pleas for aid.

sentences.zh: 會芝出城浴馬，使強與俱歸。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhi left the city to bathe horses; Mo had someone force him to return together.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi rode outside to water the horses, Mo had him seized and dragged back in.

sentences.zh: 默乃遣芝質于石勒，勒以默多詐，封默書與劉曜。

translations.literal: Mo thereupon sent Zhi as hostage to Shi Le; Shi Le, because Mo was full of deceit, sealed Mo's letter and sent it to Liu Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Mo then sent Zhi as hostage to Shi Le, who distrusted Mo and forwarded his letter sealed to Liu Yao.

sentences.zh: 默使人伺得勒書，便突圍投李矩。

translations.literal: Mo had men spy and obtain Shi Le's letter, then suddenly broke the encirclement and fled to Li Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Mo's agents intercepted Shi Le's packet; he burst the siege and fled to Li Ju.

sentences.zh: 後與矩並力距劉、石，事見矩傳。

translations.literal: Later he jointly with Ju resisted Liu and Shi—the affair is seen in Ju's biography.
translations.idiomatic: He later fought Liu Yao and the Shi alongside Li Ju, as told in Li Ju's biography.

sentences.zh: 太興初，除潁川太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taixing, he was appointed prefect of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taixing he was named prefect of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 默與石匆戰敗，矩轉蹙弱，默深憂懼，解印授其參軍殷嶠，謂之曰：「李使君遇吾甚厚，今遂棄去，無顏謝之，三日可白吾去也。

translations.literal: Mo was defeated in battle with Shi Cong; Ju turned ever weaker; Mo was deeply worried and afraid; he handed his seal to his adjutant Yin Yao, saying to him: "Prefect Li has treated me very generously; now I suddenly abandon him—I have no face to thank him; within three days you may report my departure.
translations.idiomatic: Beaten by Shi Cong while Li Ju weakened, Guo Mo panicked, handed his seal to Yin Yao, and said, "Li Ju has been generous; I cannot face him if I slip away—announce my flight in three days.

sentences.zh: 」乃奔陽翟。

translations.literal: Thereupon he fled to Yangzhai.
translations.idiomatic: He bolted for Yangzhai.

sentences.zh: 矩聞之，大怒，遣其將郭誦追默，至襄城，及之。

translations.literal: When Ju heard it, he was greatly angry, sent his general Guo Song to pursue Mo, reached Xiangcheng, and overtook him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju, enraged, sent Guo Song after him and ran him down at Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 默棄家人，單馬馳去。

translations.literal: Mo abandoned wife and children and alone on horseback galloped away.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Mo abandoned his family and galloped off alone.

sentences.zh: 默至京都，明帝授征虜將軍。

translations.literal: When Mo reached the capital district, Emperor Ming appointed him General Who Punishes Captives.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital Emperor Ming named him General Who Punishes Captives.

sentences.zh: 劉遐卒，以默為北中郎將、監淮北軍事、假節。

translations.literal: When Liu Xia died, Mo was appointed north camp general of the guard, supervisor of military affairs north of the Huai, with credential.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Xia died he became north camp general of the guard, supervisor of Huai defense, with baton of authority.

sentences.zh: 遐故部曲李龍等謀反，詔默與右衛將軍趙胤討平之。

translations.literal: Xia's old retainers Li Long and others plotted rebellion; an edict ordered Mo and guard general of the right Zhao Yin jointly to punish and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xia's old followers Li Long and others plotted revolt; the court ordered Guo Mo and Zhao Yin of the right guard to crush them.

sentences.zh: 朝廷將征蘇峻，懼其為亂，召默拜後將軍，領屯騎校尉。

translations.literal: The court was about to campaign against Su Jun and feared he would cause chaos; it summoned Mo and appointed him rear general, concurrently colonel of the encampment cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When the court moved against Su Jun it feared Guo Mo might stir trouble, so it summoned him as rear general and colonel of the camp cavalry.

sentences.zh: 初戰有功，及六軍敗績，南奔。

translations.literal: In the first battle he had merit; when the six armies were routed, he fled south.
translations.idiomatic: He fought well at first, but when the imperial host collapsed he ran south.

sentences.zh: 郗鑒議于曲阿北大業裏作壘，以分賊勢，使默守之。

translations.literal: Xi Jian deliberated on building a fort north of Qu'a at Daye village to divide the bandits' force and had Mo defend it.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jian proposed a fort north of Qu'a at Daye to split Su Jun's strength and put Guo Mo in charge of it.

sentences.zh: 峻遣韓晁等攻默甚急，壘中頗乏水，默懼，分人馬出外，乃潛從南門蕩出，留人堅守。

translations.literal: Su Jun sent Han Mian and others to attack Mo very urgently; inside the fort they were quite short of water; Mo feared, divided men and horses to go outside, then secretly slipped out from the south gate in a dash, leaving men to hold fast on defense.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun sent Han Mian to hammer the fort; water ran low and Guo Mo panicked—he slipped part of his force outside, then broke out the south gate under cover while leaving a rear guard.

sentences.zh: 會峻死，圍解，徵為右軍將軍。

translations.literal: It happened that Su Jun died; the siege was lifted; Mo was summoned as general of the right army.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Jun died the ring broke, and Guo Mo was recalled as general of the right army.

sentences.zh: 默樂為邊將，不願宿衛，及赴召，謂平南將軍劉胤曰：「我能禦胡而不見用。

translations.literal: Mo delighted in being a frontier general and did not wish to serve in palace guard; when he went to answer the summons, he said to General Who Pacifies the South Liu Yin: "I can ward off the Hu yet am not employed.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Mo preferred life on the border to palace duty. When the summons came he told General Who Pacifies the South, Liu Yin, "I can hold the steppe line yet the court will not use me.

sentences.zh: 右軍主禁兵，若疆場有虞，被使出征，方始配給，將卒無素，恩信不著，以此臨敵，少有不敗矣。

translations.literal: The general of the right army commands the forbidden troops; if the borderlands have alarm, one is ordered out on campaign, and only then are troops assigned—officers and soldiers have no prior acquaintance, favor and trust are not established—with this to face the foe, scarcely one in few will not be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The general of the right leads the household guards: if the frontier flares, he is sent out on the spur of the moment, given troops he has never led—no bond of trust—and that is how he meets the enemy. Small wonder he almost always loses.

sentences.zh: 時當為官擇才，若人臣自擇官，安得不亂乎」胤曰：「所論事雖然，非小人所及也。

translations.literal: The time ought to be that the office selects talent; if ministers themselves select office, how can there not be chaos?" Yin said: "The matters you discuss are indeed so, yet they are not what petty men can reach.
translations.idiomatic: The court should pick the man for the post, not the man the post. Let every officer choose his own job and the realm falls to ruin." Liu Yin answered, "You speak truth, but such things are above my station.

sentences.zh: 」當發，求資於胤。

translations.literal: When he was about to depart, he sought funds from Yin.
translations.idiomatic: As he prepared to leave he hit Liu Yin for travel money.

sentences.zh: 時胤被詔免官，不即歸罪，方自申理，而驕侈更甚，遠近怪之。

translations.literal: At that time Yin had received an edict removing him from office but did not at once return to answer for guilt; he was justifying himself, yet arrogance and extravagance grew still worse; near and far marveled at it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin had been dismissed but stayed on to plead his case, all the while living more arrogantly than ever; people talked from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 初，默之被征距蘇峻也，下次尋陽，見胤，胤參佐張滿等輕默，倮露視之，默常切齒。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Mo had been summoned to resist Su Jun, he next stopped at Xunyang, saw Yin; Yin's adjutants Zhang Man and others treated Mo lightly, exposed and humiliated him; Mo constantly ground his teeth.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Mo had first marched against Su Jun, he stopped at Xunyang and met Liu Yin; Zhang Man and other staffers sneered at him and made a public spectacle of his shame. Guo Mo never forgot it.

sentences.zh: 至是，胤臘日餉默酒一器，肫一頭，默對信投之水中，忿憤益甚。

translations.literal: At this time, on the la day Yin presented Mo one vessel of wine and one head of pickled shank; Mo, facing the messenger, threw them into the water; rage and resentment grew still worse.
translations.idiomatic: On the year-end la festival Liu Yin sent wine and a salted shank; Guo Mo had the courier watch as he flung the gifts into the river, his hatred sharper than ever.

sentences.zh: 又僑人蓋肫先略取祖煥所殺孔煒女為妻，煒家求之，張滿等使還其家，肫不與，因與胤、滿有隙。

translations.literal: Moreover the sojourner Gai Tun had earlier plundered and taken the daughter Kong Wei, whom Zu Huan had killed, as wife; Wei's family sought her; Zhang Man and others had her returned to her family; Tun would not give her, and therefore had a rift with Yin and Man.
translations.idiomatic: The refugee Gai Tun had earlier seized Kong Wei's daughter—Kong Wei murdered by Zu Huan—and made her his wife. Her kin demanded her back; Zhang Man forced Tun to release her, but Tun refused, which set him against Liu Yin and Zhang Man.

sentences.zh: 至是，肫謂默曰：「劉江州不受免，密有異圖，與長史司馬張滿、荀楷等日夜計謀，反逆已形，惟忌郭侯一人，-{云}-當先除郭侯而後起事。

translations.literal: At this time Tun said to Mo: "Prefect Liu of Jiangzhou has not accepted dismissal and secretly harbors a different plan; with chief clerk Zhang Man, Xun Kai, and others he plots day and night; the shape of rebellion is already formed; he only fears Marquis Guo alone—they say he will first remove Marquis Guo and afterward raise the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Then Tun told Guo Mo, "Liu Yin of Jiangzhou ignores his recall and plots treason with Zhang Man, Xun Kai, and the rest day and night. The thing is ripe; he only fears you, Lord Guo—word is he means to kill you first, then move.

sentences.zh: 禍將至矣，宜深備之。

translations.literal: Disaster is about to arrive; you should deeply prepare.
translations.idiomatic: Ruin is at hand; you must brace for it.

sentences.zh: 」默既懷恨，便率其徒候旦門開襲胤。

translations.literal: Mo, already harboring hatred, thereupon led his followers to wait until dawn when the gates opened and raided Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Burning with old grudges, Guo Mo brought his men to the yamen gates at dawn and stormed Liu Yin.

sentences.zh: 胤將吏欲距默，默呴之曰：「我被詔有所討，動者誅及三族。

translations.literal: Yin's generals and clerks wished to resist Mo; Mo rebuked them, saying: "I have received an edict to punish someone; whoever moves will be executed to the third degree of kin.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin's officers meant to fight; Guo Mo roared that he carried an imperial warrant—anyone who moved would die with three degrees of kin.

sentences.zh: 」遂入至內寢。

translations.literal: Thereupon he entered to the inner bedchamber.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed through to the private chambers.

sentences.zh: 胤尚與妾臥，默牽下斬之。

translations.literal: Yin was still lying with a concubine; Mo dragged him down and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin was still abed with a concubine; Guo Mo dragged him out and struck off his head.

sentences.zh: 出取胤僚佐張滿、荀楷等，誣以大逆。

translations.literal: He went out and seized Yin's staff Zhang Man, Xun Kai, and others, falsely accusing them of great treason.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Zhang Man, Xun Kai, and the rest of Liu Yin's staff on trumped-up charges of treason.

sentences.zh: 傳胤首于京師，詐作詔書，宜視內外。

translations.literal: He sent Yin's head to the capital, forged an edict, and proclaimed it within and without.
translations.idiomatic: He shipped Liu Yin's head to the capital, forged an edict, and had it read aloud inside and out.

sentences.zh: 掠胤女及諸妾，並金寶還船。

translations.literal: He plundered Yin's daughters and concubines together with gold and jewels and returned to his boats.
translations.idiomatic: He looted Liu Yin's daughters, concubines, and treasure and withdrew to his fleet.

sentences.zh: 初-{云}-下都，俄而還，停胤故府，招桓宣、王愆期。

translations.literal: At first they said he would go down to the capital; soon he returned, stopped at Yin's old headquarters, and summoned Huan Xuan and Wang Yanqi.
translations.idiomatic: He first announced a descent on the capital, then doubled back, occupied Liu Yin's old yamen, and called in Huan Xuan and Wang Yanqi.

sentences.zh: 愆期懼逼，勸默為平南、江州，默從之。

translations.literal: Yanqi, fearing pressure, urged Mo to take the offices General Who Pacifies the South and Jiangzhou; Mo followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanqi, afraid of being cornered, talked Guo Mo into claiming the titles General Who Pacifies the South and governor of Jiangzhou, and Mo agreed.

sentences.zh: 愆期因逃廬山，桓宣固守不應。

translations.literal: Yanqi therefore fled to Mount Lu; Huan Xuan held fast and did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanqi bolted to Mount Lu while Huan Xuan shut his gates and refused the summons.

sentences.zh: 司徒王導懼不可制，乃大赦天下，梟胤首於大航，以默為西中郎將、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Minister of education Wang Dao, fearing he could not be controlled, thereupon greatly pardoned the realm, displayed Yin's head on the Great Pontoon bridge, and appointed Mo west camp general of the guard and inspector of Yu province.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao, fearing he could not contain him, proclaimed a general amnesty, spiked Liu Yin's head on the Great Floating Bridge, and named Guo Mo west camp general of the guard and inspector of Yu province.

sentences.zh: 武昌太守鄧岳馳白太尉陶侃，侃聞之，投袂起曰：「此必詐也。

translations.literal: Wuchang prefect Deng Yue galloped to report to grand commandant Tao Kan; when Kan heard it, he cast aside his sleeve and rose, saying: "This must be a fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yue of Wuchang raced word to Tao Kan, who flung down his robe and cried, "This is a lie.

sentences.zh: 」即日率眾討默，上疏陳默罪惡。

translations.literal: That same day he led the host to punish Mo and submitted a memorial stating Mo's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: That very day he marched against Guo Mo and memorialized every crime.

sentences.zh: 導聞之，乃收胤首，詔庾亮助侃討默。

translations.literal: When Dao heard it, he thereupon took in Yin's head and ordered Yu Liang to aid Kan in punishing Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao, hearing this, recovered Liu Yin's head and ordered Yu Liang to join Tao Kan against Guo Mo.

sentences.zh: 默欲南據豫章，而侃已至城下築土山以臨之。

translations.literal: Mo wished to hold Yuzhang to the south, but Kan had already arrived below the walls and built earthen hills overlooking them.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Mo meant to slip south into Yuzhang, but Tao Kan was already below the walls throwing up siege mounds.

sentences.zh: 諸軍大集，圍之數重。

translations.literal: The various armies greatly gathered and besieged them in several layers.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial columns ringed him layer on layer.

sentences.zh: 侃惜默驍勇，欲活之，遣郭誦見默，默許降，而默將張醜、宋侯等恐為侃所殺，故致進退，不時得出。

translations.literal: Kan prized Mo's fierce courage and wished to keep him alive; he sent Guo Song to see Mo; Mo consented to surrender, but Mo's generals Zhang Chou, Song Hou, and others feared being killed by Kan, therefore caused hesitation in advancing and retreating and could not promptly come out.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan admired Guo Mo's valor and meant to spare him; he sent Guo Song to treat for surrender. Guo Mo agreed, but Zhang Chou, Song Hou, and other officers feared Tao Kan would slaughter them, so they stalled and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 攻之轉急，宋侯遂縛默求降，即斬於軍門，同黨死者四十人，傳首京師。

translations.literal: The attack grew more urgent; Song Hou thereupon bound Mo seeking surrender; he was immediately beheaded at the army gate; forty of the same faction died; the head was sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: As the assault tightened, Song Hou bound Guo Mo and offered capitulation; Tao Kan had him beheaded at the camp gate along with forty accomplices, and sent the head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 【史評】

translations.literal: Historian's appraisal
translations.idiomatic: Historian's appraisal

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：邵、李、魏、郭等諸將，契闊喪亂之辰，驅馳戎馬之際，威懷足以容眾，勇略足以制人，乃保據危城，折沖千里，招集義勇，抗禦仇讎，雖艱阻備嘗，皆乃心王室。

translations.literal: The historian says: The generals Shao, Li, Wei, Guo, and others, in the season of separation and ruin, galloping amid war-horses, had majesty and kindness enough to embrace the host, courage and strategy enough to control men; they protected and held perilous cities, repelled foes a thousand li, gathered righteous warriors, and resisted hated enemies; although hardships and obstructions were fully tasted, all bent their hearts to the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: The chronicler writes: Through collapse and exile, Shao Xu, Li Ju, Wei Jun, Guo Mo, and their like rode the storm—humane enough to hold a following, bold enough to master events. They clung to doomed towns, blunted enemies a thousand li away, rallied loyal bands, and faced down hated foes. They tasted every hardship yet kept faith with the Jin.

sentences.zh: 而矩能以少擊眾，戰勝獲多，遂使玄明憤恚，世龍挫衄。

translations.literal: Yet Ju was able with few to strike many, in battle victorious and captures many, thereby causing Xuanyuan to rage with resentment and Shilong to suffer setback.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju in particular beat larger hosts again and again, stinging Liu Yao into fury and bruising Shi Hu.

sentences.zh: 惜其寡弱，功虧一簣。

translations.literal: It is regrettable that they were few and weak and merit failed one basket short.
translations.idiomatic: They were too few and too weak, and victory slipped from their grasp at the last.

sentences.zh: 方之數子，其最優乎！

translations.literal: Compared to these several men, was he not the most excellent!
translations.idiomatic: Set beside the others, Li Ju was the finest of them all.

sentences.zh: 默既拔跡危亡，參陪朝伍，忿因眥睚，禍及誅夷，非夫狂悖，豈宜至此！

translations.literal: Mo, having pulled himself from danger and death and joined the court ranks, in resentment because of a sidelong glance brought disaster reaching execution and extermination—if he were not mad and perverse, how could it properly reach this!
translations.idiomatic: Guo Mo climbed from the wreckage into court, then murdered over a sidelong glance—only a man deranged beyond measure ends so.

sentences.zh: 段匹磾本自遐方，而系心朝廷，始則盡忠國難，終乃抗節虜廷，自蘇子卿以來，一人而已。

translations.literal: Duan Pidi originally came from a distant region yet tied his heart to the court; at first he exhausted loyalty in the state's crisis, at the end upheld integrity in the barbarian court; since Su Ziqing, there has been only one man.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Pidi was a man of the far steppe yet pinned his heart on the Jin: first he spent his loyalty in the dynasty's darkest hour, then died unbent in a barbarian court—since Su Wu there has been only one such man.

sentences.zh: 越石之見誅段氏，實以威名；

translations.literal: Yueshi's being executed by the Duan clan was truly because of awesome reputation;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun fell to the Duan blade chiefly because his fame terrified them;

sentences.zh: 匹磾之取戮世龍，亦由眾望：禍福之應，何其速哉！

translations.literal: Pidi's receiving execution at Shilong's hands was likewise because of the host's hopes: how swift were the responses of fortune and disaster!
translations.idiomatic: Duan Pidi died at Shi Hu's hands for the same reason—the expectations of the crowd. How swiftly blessing turns to bane!

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「無言不酬，無德不報」，此之謂也。

translations.literal: The Classic of Poetry says: "For no word is there no answer; for no virtue is there no recompense"—this is what it speaks of.
translations.idiomatic: As the Classic of Poetry says, "No word spoken goes unanswered; no kindness shown goes unrepaid"—here is the proof.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：邵李諸將，實惟忠壯。

translations.literal: The encomium says: The generals Shao and Li were truly loyal and stalwart.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy reads: Shao Xu and Li Ju were men of steadfast loyalty.

sentences.zh: 蒙犯艱危，驅馳亭鄣。

translations.literal: They braved hardship and peril and galloped among frontier watchtowers.
translations.idiomatic: They braved every danger and rode the border forts.

sentences.zh: 力小任重，功虧身喪。

translations.literal: Their strength was small yet their burden heavy; merit failed and their persons perished.
translations.idiomatic: Their strength was slight for the weight they bore; their work unfinished, they perished.

sentences.zh: 匹磾勁烈，隕身全節。

translations.literal: Pidi was fierce and upright; he lost his life yet preserved his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Pidi was iron to the core: he died but kept his honor whole.

sentences.zh: 默實凶殘，自貽罪戾。

translations.literal: Mo was truly fierce and cruel and brought guilt and crime on himself.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Mo was savagery itself and reaped the ruin he sowed.
